intro_feedback: The Introduction is clearly above insufficient and fits the rubric's adequate-to-good range. It presents societal relevance early, defines SAD and the treatment formats, introduces inhibitory learning as the central framework, discusses the required prior studies, and ends with a clear research question and hypothesis. The overall line of reasoning is mostly coherent and relevant. Strong points are the explicit comparison between TG-VRET, SG-VRET, and in vivo exposure, and the attempt to explain expected differences through delivery factors rather than entirely different mechanisms. The paper also does a reasonable job of using prior literature to motivate the active comparison and the hypothesis. What keeps this from a higher grade is that the argumentation is somewhat repetitive and not always sharply structured. Some claims are asserted more strongly than the cited literature seems to warrant, especially around therapist superiority and mechanism claims. There are also some inconsistencies in population focus: the introduction opens with adolescent relevance, but the study later concerns adults with SAD. That weakens the precision of the societal relevance and the alignment between opening argument and final RQ. In addition, some transitions are loose, and parts of the theory section drift into descriptive treatment explanation rather than building a tighter argument toward the hypothesis. Overall, this is a solid, mostly coherent introduction with a clear RQ, but not yet consistently convincing enough for the highest bands.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing the line of reasoning toward the research question, relevance, and hypothesis. A useful refinement would be to distinguish more explicitly between 'coherent' and 'convincingly argued' with concrete indicators such as theory integration, quality of synthesis across studies, and alignment between societal relevance and target population. At present, adjacent levels can be somewhat difficult to separate consistently.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and clearly related to the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the basic design can be followed. Important strengths are the inclusion of recruitment, inclusion and exclusion criteria, random assignment, compensation, session structure, and a reasonably clear description of the three conditions. The LSAS is described with item content, scoring, range, and a citation, which fits the expectations for this course level. The section is therefore complete enough to fall in the adequate range. However, there are several omissions and imprecisions that prevent a higher score. Participant demographics are only partially reported in the Participants section: mean age and percentage women are given, but not the full group-specific breakdown there. Some crucial methodological details are still vague, such as how exactly the in vivo tasks were implemented, whether the LSAS was administered as self-report or interview in practice, and how treatment fidelity or adherence to homework was ensured. The Materials section also mixes design information, diagnosis, intervention description, and measurement in a somewhat untidy way. In addition, some details appear inconsistent or under-justified, such as the statement that task difficulty was matched across conditions without explaining how this was standardized. So while the design is clearly understandable and mostly complete, the section is not yet fully precise or replicable.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric captures coherence and completeness well, but it could be improved by specifying a few anchor elements that are especially important at this course level, such as allocation to conditions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, operationalization of key variables, and enough procedural detail for approximate replication. That would help distinguish 'nearly complete' from 'complete' more reliably.
results_feedback: The Results section is mostly correct and relevant to the stated design, but it is only nearly complete rather than fully complete. The chosen analysis matches the design: a 3 x 2 mixed ANOVA is appropriate for comparing three conditions across pre- and post-assessment. Assumption checks are reported at an acceptable student level, and the narrative correctly interprets the significant main effect of time and the interaction. The follow-up comparisons are also mostly understandable and tied to the hypothesis. This places the section above insufficient. What lowers the grade is that the reporting is noticeably less complete than the sample structure expects. The paper refers to Table 1, Table 2, and Figure 1, but these are not properly integrated in the section as formatted tables/figures in the Results narrative. The demographics table and outcome means do appear elsewhere, but the presentation is incomplete and not fully embedded. Statistical reporting also contains some issues: the interaction is described as a 'main effect of time x condition' rather than an interaction, some APA/statistical formatting is inconsistent, and there is no effect size reporting. The post-hoc reporting is limited and does not fully unpack all comparisons in a detailed way. Overall, the analysis is appropriate and understandable, but the section falls short of the expected completeness and polish indicated by the sample results template.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric would benefit from more explicit anchors tied to the course sample, for example requiring demographics, descriptive statistics per condition/time, an analysis aligned with the design, and understandable reporting of post-hoc tests where needed. The current distinction between adequate and good is somewhat broad, and the excellent category may overemphasize advanced statistical expertise relative to this assignment level.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is one of the stronger parts of the paper. It opens with a clear restatement of the aim, research question, hypothesis, and main findings, and it correctly concludes that the hypothesis was only partly supported. The section also goes beyond mere restatement by interpreting the stronger in vivo effect and the absence of a difference between SG-VRET and TG-VRET. It connects findings back to prior studies and to inhibitory learning theory, and it includes several study-specific limitations and sensible directions for future research. This makes the reasoning mostly coherent and relevant, placing it in the good range. The strongest element is the willingness to engage with the unexpected finding that therapist-guided VRET did not outperform self-guided VRET. That kind of interpretation is important in this assignment. The limitations section is also fairly substantial and more specific than generic comments alone. What prevents a higher score is that some interpretations are still somewhat speculative and occasionally too confident relative to the data. For example, the claim that the inhibitory learning model is 'most fully realised' in real-life environments goes beyond what this design can firmly establish. Some theoretical implications are interesting but not always tightly argued from the actual measures used. There is also some redundancy across paragraphs, and parts of the discussion could distinguish more carefully between what the data show and what is inferred. Still, this is a solid and thoughtful discussion for this level.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes reasoning, conclusion, and critical reflection. It could be strengthened by explicitly naming several expected components: answering the RQ, relating findings to prior literature, discussing theory implications, addressing unexpected findings, and offering study-specific limitations and implications. That would make grading more transparent and reduce dependence on assessor interpretation.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language, but there are enough language, style, and APA issues to keep this in the developing-to-adequate range rather than good. The overall structure of the paper is recognizable and most sections are organized logically. The reader can follow the argument, and most paragraphs have a discernible topic. However, there are frequent grammar, spelling, punctuation, capitalization, and phrasing issues throughout the text. Examples include inconsistent capitalization, missing spaces, incorrect verb forms, awkward sentence construction, and repeated small errors such as 'then' instead of 'than', 'assesment', and inconsistent condition labels. APA style is also inconsistent in several places, including citation formatting, reference list accuracy, and bibliographic consistency. The reference list contains multiple clearly irrelevant sources for this paper, which weakens the professionalism of the presentation. There is also some redundancy and some vague wording in crucial argumentative passages. These problems do not block understanding, but they do reduce clarity and precision. Therefore the writing is passable and mostly clear, but not polished.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is useful but quite broad. It may help to separate writing clarity/structure from APA/formatting more explicitly, because a paper can be readable yet weak in APA, or vice versa. In addition, the phrase 'scientific language' could be operationalized with examples such as precision, paragraph focus, and appropriate hedging, which would improve consistency across graders.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and relevant topic, a recognizable line toward the research question, and responsible use of the core literature overall. Societal relevance is established early and the paper defines SAD, relapse, VRET, and in vivo exposure in a way that supports the topic. The theoretical framework is also present: inhibitory learning and expectancy violation are used to explain why exposure should work and why delivery format might matter. The research question and hypothesis are clearly stated and aligned with the comparison the study later tests. Stronger points are the explicit contrast between TG-VRET, SG-VRET, and in vivo exposure, and the attempt to use prior studies as building blocks toward the gap. However, the reasoning is only somewhat convincingly argued in places rather than fully tight. The introduction contains some repetition, and the logic occasionally overstates what prior studies can conclude, especially about therapist superiority and mechanism claims. Some study descriptions are simplified or slightly inaccurate, and the target population shifts: the text starts with adolescence as a major framing device, but the actual study is on adults, which weakens coherence. The argument remains understandable and relevant, but the storyline could be more streamlined and better aligned with the final design.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the key construct well by focusing on the line of reasoning toward scientific relevance, the research question, and the hypothesis. A possible improvement would be to make the distinction more explicit between 'coherent' and 'convincingly argued,' because those categories can overlap and leave room for subjective interpretation. It may also help to include explicit mention of literature synthesis versus study-by-study summary, since that is central in this assignment and strongly emphasized in the writing guide.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and clearly related to the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, treatment conditions, and the overall design are understandable, and the section includes several required elements: inclusion and exclusion criteria, recruitment source, random allocation, compensation, age, and gender distribution. The interventions are described in a way that makes the intended comparison between conditions clear, and the LSAS is explained with enough detail for this course level, including item structure, scoring range, and cutoff. Procedure is chronological and understandable. The section is therefore adequately complete and mostly correct. At the same time, it lacks some specificity needed for stronger replicability. Important sample details are only given for the full sample rather than fully by condition in the prose, and some intervention descriptions remain fairly general. There is also some mixing of design/procedure/materials information across subsections. The Methods mention matched dose and difficulty, but do not explain clearly how equivalence across in vivo and VR tasks was ensured in practice. In addition, the study uses a repeated-measures design but provides no follow-up despite the introduction emphasizing maintenance and relapse. Overall this is a solid student-level methods section, but not yet fully comprehensive.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is useful in emphasizing coherence between design, RQ, and hypotheses, and completeness of participants, materials, and procedures. To improve reliability, it could specify key required elements more concretely for this course context, such as allocation procedure, inclusion/exclusion criteria, sample characteristics, and sufficient operational detail for replication. The current wording risks compressing many different types of omissions into one broad judgment.
results_feedback: The Results section is mostly coherent and broadly matches the stated design, but it is less complete than expected relative to the sample results template. A suitable mixed ANOVA was chosen for the 3-group by 2-time design, assumptions are addressed at an acceptable student level, and the main findings are reported in a generally understandable way. The interpretation of the interaction is also clear and relevant to the hypothesis. However, the section is weakened by missing formal presentation of the descriptive tables and figure within the Results text itself: Table 1 and Table 2 are announced but not actually properly integrated in the section, and the reporting relies on labels rather than full formatted presentation. The interaction is referred to as a 'main effect of time x condition,' which is conceptually imprecise. Reporting is also somewhat incomplete because post-hoc comparisons are only partially elaborated and no exact descriptive comparison strategy is shown beyond selected p-values. Although the appended numbers make the intended results understandable, the Results section itself falls somewhat below the sample-based benchmark for completeness and structure. The analyses are mostly correct, but the reporting is only nearly complete.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric appropriately prioritizes correctness, completeness, coherence, and relevance to the stated design. It could be improved by making the expected student-level reporting standards more concrete, especially because this assignment provides a sample Results section. For example, the rubric could explicitly mention descriptive tables, reporting of assumption checks, alignment between hypotheses and analyses, and presentation of post-hoc tests. That would reduce ambiguity between an 'adequate' and 'good' score.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion presents a clear main conclusion, answers the research question, and appropriately states that the hypothesis was only partly supported. It does more than restate the results: it interprets the stronger in vivo effect and the lack of difference between SG-VRET and TG-VRET, and it relates these findings back to previous research and the inhibitory learning framework. The section also includes several relevant limitations, such as lack of follow-up, limited tailoring, missing homework adherence data, and reduced ecological validity of VR. Future research suggestions mostly follow logically from the findings and limitations, and the paper returns to societal relevance in the conclusion. These are strong features for this level. The main reason the section does not score higher is that some interpretations go beyond what the data can firmly support. For example, the argument that the virtual format itself imposes a ceiling is plausible, but remains speculative. Some references to theory are useful, though the discussion sometimes treats the inhibitory learning model in a broad and assertive way without distinguishing clearly between what was directly tested and what was inferred. Still, the reasoning is correct, mostly coherent, and relevant, with a clear argumentative thread.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric correctly emphasizes the reasoning toward the main conclusion and the relevance of the critical reflection. A useful refinement would be to separate interpretation of findings, integration with theory/literature, and critical evaluation into more visibly distinct criteria. At present, a paper can be strong in one but weaker in another, and the single rubric statement may not make those trade-offs sufficiently transparent for consistent grading.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language, but the writing quality is uneven. Most sections have a recognizable structure and the reader can follow the argument, yet there are many sentence-level language issues: grammar errors, punctuation problems, capitalization inconsistencies, awkward phrasing, and spelling mistakes. APA style is also inconsistent, with errors in in-text citations, reference formatting, article years, and reference relevance. There are also some vague or imprecise statements and a fair amount of redundancy, especially in the introduction and discussion. Paragraphing is mostly functional, but some paragraphs try to do too much at once. Because the text remains readable and the scientific meaning is usually recoverable, the language does not impede understanding; however, the number of style and APA issues is clearly more than 'few.' This places the section in the developing-to-adequate range, leaning adequate but not fully there.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and helpful, especially because it includes structure, clarity, grammar, ambiguity, redundancy, and APA. One improvement would be to distinguish more clearly between errors that affect readability and errors that are mainly formal. In student papers at this level, many texts are understandable despite frequent APA inconsistencies, so a more explicit weighting within this rubric could support more consistent grading.

intro_feedback: The Introduction presents a clear and relevant research question and gives a generally coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and hypothesis. A clear strength is that the paper distinguishes the three delivery formats and tries to connect them through the inhibitory learning framework. The selected prior studies are relevant and mostly used responsibly to motivate the comparison. The hypothesis is explicit and logically derived from the argument. However, the argumentation is somewhat uneven. The societal relevance starts strongly but becomes long and repetitive, and the target population shifts from adolescents in the opening paragraph to adults in the actual study, which weakens coherence. Some theoretical claims are stated too confidently without being fully developed, and the review sometimes becomes study-by-study summary rather than a tighter synthesis. There are also a few imprecise or awkward formulations that blur the logic. Overall, this is a solid, above-average Introduction for this course level, but not yet consistently convincing enough for a higher mark.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the key construct well: line of reasoning toward relevance, RQ, and hypothesis. A useful improvement would be to distinguish more explicitly between literature summary and literature synthesis, because students can appear 'coherent' while still writing article-by-article summaries. It may also help to mention alignment between population, theory, and final RQ as a separate indicator, since this is a common student-level issue not fully visible in the current wording.
methods_feedback: The Method section is coherent and clearly related to the research question and hypothesis. The overall design is understandable, the conditions are distinguishable, and the participants, materials, and procedure are mostly complete. Key strengths are the inclusion of diagnostic screening, explicit random allocation, basic demographics, compensation, session structure, and a reasonably clear description of the intervention logic. The LSAS is described in useful detail, including scoring and interpretation. At the same time, there are several omissions that keep the section around adequate rather than clearly strong. Important sample details are incomplete at subgroup level in the main Participants section, and gender is only reported for the full sample rather than integrated cleanly with condition allocation. Some intervention details remain too general for replication, especially how in vivo exposure was implemented session by session and how matching of task difficulty across formats was ensured. The Procedure is clear in sequence but relatively brief, and the analyses subsection is effectively absent as a dedicated component. Overall, the section is mostly correct and sufficiently complete for this level, but lacks some precision and organization expected for a higher grade.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is workable but fairly broad. It would be improved by specifying the minimum expected components more concretely, such as participant characteristics, allocation, materials/measures, procedure, and analysis plan. At present, a paper can seem 'complete' under the rubric while still omitting practically important details for replication. Adding clearer anchors for what counts as 'complete and correct' at this student level would likely improve grading consistency.
results_feedback: The Results section reports an analysis that matches the stated design and is mostly understandable. The mixed ANOVA is appropriate for the design, assumptions are addressed, and the reporting includes main effects, the interaction, and post-hoc comparisons. The interpretation of the interaction is also generally correct. However, the section is notably less complete than the sample structure expects. The demographic and descriptive tables are referred to but not properly formatted within the Results narrative, and some essential statistical reporting is missing or underdeveloped. The interaction is called a 'main effect of time x condition,' which is conceptually imprecise. There is no full reporting of the descriptive statistics directly in table form as expected, and the post-hoc comparisons are selective and not always fully tied to the hypothesis. The statement about the overall main effect of condition averaged across time is not very informative and could be misleading in the presence of a strong interaction. In addition, the Results section is short and somewhat schematic compared with the course sample. Overall, the analysis is mostly correct, but reporting is only nearly complete and somewhat less polished than average.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric rightly focuses on correctness, completeness, coherence, and relevance, but the distinction between 'Adequate' and 'Good' could be sharper. Because this course uses a sample Results section as a benchmark, the rubric could benefit from explicitly naming expected elements such as a demographics table, descriptive outcome table, assumption checks, main analysis, and post-hoc tests. That would make it easier to separate papers that are statistically appropriate but underreported from those that are fully developed.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion gives a clear main conclusion, answers the research question, and correctly states that the hypothesis was only partly supported. A major strength is that the student does not ignore the unexpected finding that self-guided and therapist-guided VRET did not differ, and instead attempts to explain it in relation to prior literature and theory. The section also links the findings back to the inhibitory learning model and includes several study-specific limitations and future directions. The broader implications are sensible and tied back to accessibility and treatment delivery. What keeps the Discussion from a higher mark is that some interpretations are more speculative than well-supported by the actual data. The argument that the virtual format imposed a 'ceiling' is plausible but not directly tested, and some claims about ecological validity and expectancy violation are presented rather strongly. There is also some repetition, and certain limitations are generic or phrased somewhat loosely. Still, this is a coherent and reasonably well-argued Discussion that goes beyond merely restating the results and fits well within the expected level for a first research paper.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes main conclusion and critical reflection, but it could be strengthened by explicitly including integration with theory and prior research. At present, students might receive similar scores whether they simply restate findings and list limitations or whether they truly interpret findings in relation to the Introduction. Making the expectation for explanation of unexpected findings more explicit would also improve alignment with the course goals.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the scientific tone is mostly appropriate, but language and style issues occur often enough to affect clarity. The structure at section level is clear, and most paragraphs have a recognizable focus. However, there are many grammar, spelling, capitalization, and punctuation problems, including sentence fragments, inconsistent tense, awkward phrasing, and article/preposition errors. APA style is inconsistent in several places, with citation inaccuracies, formatting issues, and clear problems in the reference list. There are also some vague or imprecise formulations in crucial argumentative passages. The paper remains understandable, but the writing is not yet consistently polished. This fits a below-to-around-average score for Language & Style rather than a strong one.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and useful, especially because it balances clarity, structure, grammar, APA, and redundancy. One challenge is that it combines many dimensions into a single criterion, which can make holistic scoring variable between assessors. It might help to provide brief anchor examples for what distinguishes 'some errors' from 'few errors' and to clarify how much APA problems should weigh relative to clarity and structure in this course context.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and the final research question. The societal relevance is present early and is linked to access to treatment, relapse, and delivery format, which fits the assignment well. Key concepts such as SAD, exposure, inhibitory learning, TG-VRET, SG-VRET, and in vivo exposure are defined sufficiently for this level. The research question and hypothesis are clearly stated and logically follow from the preceding argument.

The strongest aspect is that the paper does more than simply list articles: the four required studies are all included, and most are used as building blocks toward the comparison of delivery formats. The Introduction also makes a genuine attempt to connect theory to design by arguing that all conditions rely on expectancy violation and inhibitory learning, so observed differences should reflect delivery factors.

The main limitation is that the synthesis is only partly consistent. Some paragraphs are strong and comparative, but others drift into summary. A few claims are stated too confidently based on limited evidence, especially the conclusion that therapist involvement enhances outcomes and that SG-VRET "confirms" activation of the same core mechanisms. Some wording is also imprecise or overstated, which weakens the soundness of a few links in the argument. In addition, the opening frames adolescence as important, but the actual study concerns adults; that creates a mismatch in the societal relevance paragraph. Overall, though, the argumentative flow is clear and mostly coherent, placing this in the adequate range rather than clearly good.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing line of reasoning, synthesis, relevance, and the connection between prior research and the RQ. A useful refinement would be to separate more explicitly between completeness requirements and quality of synthesis. Right now, the criteria bundle presence of components and argumentative quality together, which can make it harder to distinguish a complete-but-summary-based introduction from a genuinely well-synthesized one. It may also help to operationalize what counts as meaningful synthesis with one or two concrete indicators.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section describes a coherent study design that matches the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the basic design is understandable and replicable at a student level. Important participant information is included: age range, diagnostic confirmation, key exclusion criteria, recruitment source, random assignment, and compensation. The intervention conditions are described clearly enough to understand what differs between them and what was standardized across them.

The Materials section also gives an adequate description of the main dependent measure, including item count, response scale, scoring, score range, cutoff, and a brief validity statement. This aligns reasonably well with the writing guide. The Procedure is chronological and easy to follow.

The main weaknesses are missing or underdeveloped details rather than conceptual confusion. For example, the sample description does not report standard deviation for age and gives gender only as a percentage rather than per condition, which the guide expects. Some details that would strengthen replicability are still vague, such as how exactly in vivo scenarios were implemented, who delivered the therapist-guided protocol, whether assessors were blinded, and how homework adherence was handled. There is also some mixing of conceptual and procedural information across sections, and the analysis plan is not explicitly described as a separate subsection. Still, the design is coherent and mostly complete, so this fits the adequate band.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately focuses on coherence, completeness, and correct placement of information. It could be improved by specifying a few anchor details from the writing guide that are especially important for student-level grading, such as allocation procedure, key demographics, intervention comparability, and enough detail for rough replication. At present, the jump between bands can feel broad, especially between adequate and good, because "complete and correct" is somewhat open to interpretation.
results_feedback:
The Results section is generally aligned with the stated design and uses an appropriate mixed ANOVA for the 3 x 2 design. Assumption checks are mentioned, the main effects and interaction are reported with test statistics, degrees of freedom, and p-values, and post-hoc comparisons are described. The interpretation of the interaction is understandable and matches the descriptive pattern shown in the provided tables.

However, compared with the sample results structure, the section is somewhat incomplete. The tables and figure are referenced, but within the written Results section they are not properly integrated in full academic form; instead, the actual table content appears only later in the paper and not formatted as full tables in place. The sample expects demographics and descriptive statistics tables clearly presented, and ideally a graphical display. The reporting is therefore only partly complete. In addition, there is a small wording error in describing the interaction as a "main effect of time x condition," which is statistically imprecise. The discussion of post-hoc comparisons is understandable, but somewhat thin, and does not fully unpack all relevant pairwise patterns at the level shown in the sample.

Because the analysis is mostly correct and coherent but one or two expected reporting elements are missing or poorly implemented, this fits the lower end of the adequate band.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric benefits from the accompanying sample, which gives concrete expectations. That said, the rubric itself could more explicitly distinguish between statistical correctness and reporting completeness. For example, missing tables/figures versus minor imprecision in wording are currently grouped together. Adding explicit anchors for descriptive tables, assumption checks, interaction reporting, and post-hoc comparisons would make grading more consistent across assessors.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion has a clear main conclusion, directly answers the research question, and states that the hypothesis was only partly supported. The findings are summarized accurately at construct level, and the section generally keeps returning to the central issue of comparative effectiveness across delivery formats. This is a strong feature.

The paper also does a good job of comparing the findings to prior research. The discussion links the overall reduction in symptoms to the earlier VRET and in vivo literature, and it meaningfully addresses the unexpected lack of difference between SG-VRET and TG-VRET. Importantly, the student does not ignore this unexpected result but proposes explanations grounded in design differences and ecological validity. The inhibitory learning model is brought back into the interpretation, and the discussion attempts to refine the theory rather than merely restating it.

The limitations section is study-specific and reasonably convincing: lack of follow-up, standardization possibly reducing tailoring, limited realism of VR, unmonitored homework adherence, and reliance on self-report are all relevant. Future directions mostly follow logically from these limitations and from the findings.

The main reason this is not higher is that some theoretical interpretations are still somewhat overstated. For example, the claim that the results "specify" the inhibitory learning model is interesting but stronger than the data can firmly support. Some arguments could also be more tightly linked to specific findings rather than broader speculation. Even so, for this course level the Discussion is above average: coherent, interpretive, and clearly connected to the Introduction.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the most important elements well: conclusion, interpretation, linkage to introduction, limitations, and future research. A useful refinement would be to make explicit that students should engage with unexpected findings rather than only restating expected ones, since this is a key quality marker in this assignment. It may also help to distinguish more clearly between generic implications and implications that follow directly from the obtained results.
lang_style_feedback:
The overall language is understandable and generally scientific in tone, and the structure of major sections is clear. Most paragraphs have a discernible topic, and terminology is mostly consistent across the paper. The reader can follow the intended argument without major difficulty.

That said, there are enough language and APA issues to keep this in the adequate rather than good range. There are repeated grammar, capitalization, punctuation, and spelling errors, such as sentence fragments, missing commas or periods, inconsistent capitalization, agreement errors, and typos. There are also several APA/reference problems: inconsistent citation formatting, inaccurate reference details, missing or incomplete source information, and inclusion of clearly irrelevant references in the reference list. Some phrasing is vague or awkward, and a few sentences are overly long or imprecise. The results tables are also not cleanly integrated into the paper format.

These issues do not usually impede understanding, but they are noticeable and frequent enough that the writing is satisfactory rather than polished.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and helpful, especially in protecting content grades from being overly penalized for writing issues. One improvement would be to clarify how to weigh APA/reference errors versus broader readability and structure, since the current wording lists many possible error types without indicating their relative importance. The thresholds based on counting errors are practical, but they may still benefit from examples of what counts as a distinct error type.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and finally the research question and hypothesis. The societal relevance is present early and reasonably well connected to treatment accessibility and relapse risk. Key concepts such as SAD, VRET, in vivo exposure, inhibitory learning, and expectancy violation are defined and linked to the study. The required core studies are included, as well as an additional article relevant to self-guided VRET. A major strength is that the paper does more than merely list studies; there is some synthesis, especially in the move toward comparing delivery formats. The research question is clear and the hypothesis follows from the preceding argument.

The section is not stronger because parts of the reasoning remain somewhat uneven. Some claims are overstated or insufficiently supported, for example the idea that all differences are most likely due only to delivery factors, or that self-guided VRET necessarily offers a higher dose. Some transitions are also a bit abrupt, and the target population shifts: the introduction opens with adolescent relevance but the actual study concerns adults with SAD. That weakens coherence. In addition, some comparisons of prior research are slightly simplified, and the theory is used more as a general framing device than as a tightly developed explanatory framework that directly motivates each prediction. Overall, this fits the good range: coherent, relevant, and mostly well-argued, with a few weaker links.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing argumentation, synthesis, and the need for a clear line toward the research question. A useful refinement would be to operationalize more clearly how assessors should weigh missing required content versus weaker synthesis when both are present to some degree. The criterion about 'all four core articles' is concrete, but the phrase 'one component may be written relatively poorly' still leaves room for substantial assessor variation. It may help to include anchor examples of what counts as description versus genuine synthesis at this student level.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section describes a coherent design that matches the research question: a three-condition comparison of treatment formats with pre- and post-assessment of social anxiety symptoms. The Participants section includes inclusion and exclusion criteria, recruitment, random assignment, compensation, and basic demographics. Materials and Procedure are separated appropriately, and the LSAS is described with useful detail on items, response format, scoring, and interpretation. The treatment conditions are explained clearly enough for this course level, and there is a visible attempt to standardize dosage and task difficulty across conditions.

The grade is not higher because several important details are still missing or underdeveloped. The participant information does not provide a standard deviation for age, which the writing guide explicitly expects. Gender is only given as an overall percentage in the Methods, while condition-specific descriptive information appears later outside the section. The SCID-5 is named but not really described as a measure. The methods also lack a separate analyses subsection, even though the results make clear that a mixed ANOVA was planned. Some treatment details remain too broad for replication, such as how scenario intensity was matched across in vivo and VR conditions, who delivered the in vivo exposure, and whether assessors were blind. These are not fatal flaws for this level, but they do leave one or two important omissions, placing the section in the adequate range.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately focuses on coherence with the research question and on completeness relative to the writing guide. It could be improved by specifying a few anchor omissions that should count as 'important details,' such as missing allocation procedure, missing demographic variability, absent analysis plan, or unclear operationalization of the intervention. At present, the difference between developing and adequate can depend heavily on assessor judgment because 'multiple important details' versus 'one or two important details' is somewhat subjective.
results_feedback:
The Results section is understandable and generally aligned with the stated design. It reports the mixed ANOVA, includes assumption checks, gives test statistics with degrees of freedom and p-values, and interprets the main effects and interaction in plain language. The reported pattern is consistent with the design and with the later discussion. That said, this section falls below the expected sample-based standard for this assignment.

Most importantly, the required descriptive elements are incomplete inside the Results narrative itself. Table 1 and Table 2 are only placeholders in the section rather than fully presented there, and the figure is also just referred to rather than properly shown and integrated. The actual numerical table content appears detached at the very end of the paper instead of being embedded as a conventional Results presentation. In addition, there is no full reporting of post-hoc comparisons across all relevant condition contrasts and time-point differences at the expected level of detail from the sample. For instance, the section reports no pairwise comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET at pre-test, and the wording around the main effect of condition risks overinterpretation because averaging across time points is not itself substantively very informative in a pre-post treatment design. There are also several reporting and formatting inconsistencies. Because the section is somewhat correct and coherent but misses one or two major sample-based elements, it fits the developing range rather than adequate.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric benefits from the comparison to the sample results and from naming concrete expected elements such as tables, interaction tests, post-hoc tests, and a figure. A possible improvement would be to distinguish more explicitly between incomplete reporting of required elements and incorrect statistical reasoning, since those can currently end up in the same band despite being different problems. It may also help to specify whether placeholder tables or detached table content should count as missing elements or merely weak presentation.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion is one of the stronger parts of the paper. It clearly restates the aim, answers the research question, and indicates that the hypothesis was only partly supported. The main findings are interpreted rather than merely repeated. The section links results back to prior studies and to the inhibitory learning framework, and it does engage with the unexpected pattern that therapist-guided and self-guided VRET did not differ. That is an important strength according to the rubric. The limitations are mostly study-specific rather than generic, and the future research suggestions often follow logically from those limitations.

The section does not receive a higher grade because some interpretations go beyond what the data can support. For example, the conclusion that the inhibitory learning model is most fully realized in real-life settings is plausible but stronger than the present design can establish. Some explanations are speculative, such as the proposed ceiling imposed by the virtual format, and these are not always weighed against alternative explanations equally carefully. There is also occasional slippage between discussing findings and treating them as if they were more definitive than a simple literature-review-based student design warrants. Still, the discussion is coherent, linked back to the introduction, meaningfully interprets results, and provides relevant limitations and implications. That places it in the good range.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the most important dimensions well: conclusion, comparison with prior research, theory integration, critical reflection, and implications. A helpful refinement would be to make clearer how to judge speculative interpretation. For example, the rubric could explicitly differentiate between reasonable, data-linked speculation and overclaiming beyond the results. That would support more consistent grading, especially because discussion quality often depends on subtle distinctions between interpretation and unsupported inference.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally readable and the intended argument is usually understandable. Terminology is mostly consistent, sectioning is clear, and the reader can follow the broad structure from introduction to conclusion. However, the writing contains frequent grammar, punctuation, capitalization, spacing, and wording errors. There are also multiple APA issues in both in-text citations and the reference list, and the layout is inconsistent. Some sentences are awkward or run-on, and several wording choices are imprecise enough to weaken clarity, though usually not to the point of making the content incomprehensible.

Examples of recurring issues include inconsistent capitalization of conditions and constructs, citation inaccuracies, spelling errors, punctuation problems, and non-APA formatting of tables and references. There is also some redundancy and some vague phrasing in important places. Because these problems are too frequent for the adequate band but do not usually obstruct understanding, the section fits the developing range.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language and Style rubric is practical and appropriately prevents language issues from overly affecting content grades. It could be improved by clarifying how to count 'different errors' in grammar or APA, since this can be interpreted inconsistently across assessors. The rubric might also benefit from more explicit attention to structural clarity across sections, not only sentence-level correctness, because signposting and paragraph focus are especially relevant for student scientific writing.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning and includes the major required components: societal relevance, theoretical framework, the three core studies, one additional study, and a research question with hypothesis. The topic is introduced in a societally relevant way, and the inhibitory learning model is used as the main theoretical basis. The paper also generally succeeds in moving from broad relevance to a more specific comparison of delivery formats. This places the section solidly in the adequate range.

What keeps it from the good range is that the synthesis is uneven. Several paragraphs summarize studies one by one rather than consistently using them as building blocks in a tightly connected argument. The theoretical reasoning is present, but some claims are stronger than the evidence provided, for example the implication that therapist involvement is already clearly established as superior before the current study, when the literature described does not fully justify that conclusion. The target population is also not fully consistent: the introduction begins with adolescence as a key focus, but the actual study concerns adults with SAD. That weakens the coherence of the societal relevance paragraph and its connection to the eventual research question. In addition, some transitions are abrupt and a few conceptual distinctions are underdeveloped, such as how delivery format differences specifically affect inhibitory learning.

Overall, the section has a sound and mostly coherent argument, but not enough consistent synthesis and precision to reach a higher score.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing argumentation, synthesis, and the connection between prior literature and the research question. A useful refinement would be to make explicit how to handle partial mismatch between societal relevance and the actual target population, since that is a common student issue. It may also help to distinguish more clearly between merely mentioning theory and actually using theory to justify hypotheses, because that difference is central but currently somewhat implicit across bands.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section is coherent and clearly related to the research question and hypotheses. The basic study design is understandable: participants, allocation, treatment conditions, outcome measure, and procedure are all described. Important elements such as random assignment, inclusion and exclusion criteria, compensation, session structure, and the main dependent variable are present. At this student level, that supports an adequate grade.

The main limitations concern completeness and precision. Participant information is somewhat limited: mean age and gender proportion are given, but standard deviation for age is missing in the main Participants text, and group-specific demographics are not integrated into the section itself in a polished way. The Materials section identifies the LSAS and gives useful scoring information, but the reference to the developers is incomplete, and the distinction between the LSAS as self-report and the usual clinician-administered version is not handled very clearly. Some descriptions are also slightly mixed across subsections, with design information, manipulation details, and procedural elements blending together. Replication would be possible only at a moderate level because several practical details remain vague, such as the exact content and progression of sessions, how task difficulty was matched, and how homework adherence was handled.

Overall, the method is mostly complete and correct, but it lacks one or two important details and finer precision expected for a stronger score.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric gives appropriate weight to coherence, completeness, and correct placement of information. A possible improvement would be to specify a small checklist of minimally required details for Participants, Materials, Procedure, and Analyses, so graders can distinguish more consistently between 'one or two important details missing' and 'multiple important details missing.' It may also help to clarify how to grade operationalization issues when the chosen measure is appropriate but described imprecisely.
results_feedback:
The Results section is understandable and the chosen analysis broadly matches the stated design. The student reports descriptives, assumption checks, main effects, an interaction, and post-hoc comparisons. This shows awareness of the expected sample-based structure and keeps the section above insufficient.

However, compared with the assignment requirements and sample results format, the section is incomplete. The tables and figure are referred to but not properly presented within the Results section itself; instead, the numerical information appears detached at the very end of the paper. The Results should contain clear demographic and outcome tables in the section, and this expectation is only partially met. Reporting is also somewhat inconsistent and imprecise. For example, the interaction is incorrectly referred to as a "main effect of time x condition," and the post-hoc reporting remains limited. There are no reported test statistics for post-hoc comparisons, and the presentation of means and standard deviations is not fully integrated into the narrative. The section also omits some expected detail for this course level, such as a more explicit descriptive overview of all groups over time in table form and a cleaner distinction between demographic descriptives and outcome descriptives.

So while the analysis is mostly relevant and partly complete, one or two important expected elements are missing or poorly executed, which fits the developing range.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is useful because it anchors expectations to the sample results section. It would be even stronger if it explicitly separated completeness of required elements from correctness of interpretation and statistical terminology. For example, students may choose the right analysis but still omit tables or mislabel interactions. Making those dimensions more explicit could improve consistency across graders.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion is the strongest section. It begins with a clear restatement of the aim, answers the research question, and explains that the hypothesis was only partly supported. The student interprets the overall pattern of findings rather than merely repeating the results. There is meaningful comparison with prior studies, especially in relation to Kampmann et al., Anderson et al., Bouchard et al., and Zainal et al. The section also returns to the inhibitory learning framework and attempts to explain what the findings imply for that theory. This level of integration supports a good score.

The critical reflection is also reasonably strong and study-specific. The student identifies relevant limitations such as the lack of follow-up, limited tailoring, imperfect ecological validity of VR, unmonitored homework adherence, and dependence on self-report. Future research suggestions generally follow from these limitations and from the findings themselves. The broader implications are also brought back at the end, which aligns well with the writing guide.

What prevents an even higher score is that some interpretations remain somewhat overstated. For example, the conclusion that the inhibitory learning model is "most fully realised" in real-life environments goes beyond what this design can strictly establish. Some explanatory claims are plausible but speculative, especially regarding ecological validity and the supposed ceiling of the virtual format. In addition, the discussion could connect findings to the theoretical framework more precisely by distinguishing what was directly tested from what was inferred.

Overall, this is a coherent, well-structured discussion with meaningful interpretation and relevant limitations, placing it in the good range.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately prioritizes interpretation, linkage to theory, and study-specific critical reflection. A helpful refinement would be to state more explicitly how much speculation is acceptable when students interpret unexpected findings. Many student discussions are plausible but overconfident, and the rubric could better distinguish evidence-based interpretation from unsupported extrapolation while still accounting for this course level.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally readable and the intended meaning is usually clear, but the language and style are inconsistent enough to lower the score into the developing range. The text has a recognizable academic structure, and most sections and paragraphs are distinguishable. Terminology is mostly understandable, and the paper generally uses scientific language appropriate for this level.

At the same time, there are repeated grammar, spelling, punctuation, and capitalization issues throughout the paper. Examples include missing commas or periods, incorrect capitalization, subject-verb issues, awkward phrasing, repeated typo-level errors, and inconsistent formatting of terms and abbreviations. APA style is also inconsistent, with problems in in-text citations, reference formatting, author-year presentation, and the reference list including multiple irrelevant sources. Some sentences are overly long or loosely connected, which occasionally weakens clarity. There are also places where terminology is not fully consistent, and several awkward formulations make the writing less polished than adequate-level work.

Because understanding is not seriously obstructed, the section does not fall below passing, but the number and frequency of style and APA issues make a score in the developing range most appropriate.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language and Style rubric is detailed and practical, especially in distinguishing clarity from mere correctness. One improvement would be to clarify how to weigh APA/reference-list problems when they are numerous but do not affect comprehension. It may also be useful to separate grammar/spelling from broader academic style and structure, because some papers are readable but mechanically error-prone, while others are grammatically cleaner but poorly organized.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and generally coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, previous research, and the research question. The paper does a good job explaining why social anxiety disorder in adolescents is important, why exposure-based treatment is relevant, and why VRET might be especially suitable for this age group. Key concepts such as avoidance, safety behaviors, habituation, and inhibitory learning are explained clearly and linked to the treatment rationale. The research question and hypotheses are explicit and logically follow from the preceding argument. The literature use is mostly responsible and the additional adolescent-focused article strengthens the relevance of the proposed study. A weaker point is that the literature synthesis is still somewhat study-by-study rather than fully integrative, and the argument for why VRET should outperform iVET is plausible but not fully developed empirically. There are also a few inaccuracies in the use of the required literature, such as citing Bouchard as 2016 instead of 2017 and describing prior studies somewhat broadly. Still, for this course level, the Introduction is above average: coherent, relevant, and convincingly argued overall.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric appropriately emphasizes the line of reasoning toward the research question, relevance, and hypothesis. A useful refinement would be to distinguish more explicitly between 'literature summary' and 'literature synthesis,' since many student papers fall in between those categories. It may also help to include a criterion about how clearly theory is integrated into the argument rather than merely mentioned, because this is central in the writing guide but only implicit in the rubric wording.
methods_feedback: The Methods section presents a coherent design that matches the research question: a three-condition comparison with pre- and post-measurement. Participants, intervention conditions, and procedure are described in a reasonably understandable way, and the general setup is replicable at a basic level. Strengths include the inclusion and exclusion criteria, sample size, age, and an attempt to describe both interventions in relation to each other. However, the section misses several elements expected by the writing guide. Participant information is incomplete: there is no gender breakdown in the main text, no clear allocation procedure beyond 'randomly assigned,' and no reward/compensation information. The diagnostic instrument is also described unclearly: 'DSM-5 Childhood Disorders (SCID-5 Junior)' is not presented accurately enough. The Materials section contains procedural details, while Procedure remains too brief and omits practical chronological detail. The iVET condition is underdescribed compared to VRET, which makes the comparability of conditions less clear. The LSAS-CA description is mostly solid, but details such as the exact scoring and cut-off rationale could be more precise. Overall, the method is adequate but not fully complete.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric captures coherence with the RQ and completeness of participants, materials, and procedure, but it remains fairly broad. It would be helpful if the rubric specified a few anchor elements drawn from the writing guide, such as allocation to conditions, inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographic details, operationalization of the IVs and DVs, and enough procedural detail for basic replication. That would make grading more transparent and consistent across assessors.
results_feedback: The Results section contains the intended structure of assumption checks, ANOVA, post-hoc tests, and references to tables and a figure, but the execution is weak and only just sufficient. A major problem is the presentation of the descriptive statistics: Table 1 and Table 2 are referred to in the text, but the formatting is incomplete and the demographic/descriptive information is confusingly placed at the very end of the paper. Table 1 even appears to include four columns with a duplicated iVET entry, which creates uncertainty about the actual sample description. The ANOVA reporting is also inconsistent with the stated design and sample size. With 120 participants in a 3x2 mixed design, the reported degrees of freedom, such as F(1, 357) and F(2, 357), do not fit the described analysis. In the post-hoc section, the text states that there were no significant pre-treatment differences, but then reports p = .007 for two of those comparisons, which would normally indicate significance. This is a substantial internal inconsistency. On the positive side, the section is organized in the expected order and the overall pattern of findings is interpretable. However, because several core statistical details are inconsistent or incorrect, the section falls at the lower bound of passing.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is serviceable but could be more specific for this assignment. Since the calibration summary and sample results strongly emphasize demographics tables, descriptive outcome tables, assumption checks, and post-hoc reporting, the rubric could explicitly mention these expected components. It would also help to clarify how heavily internal inconsistencies in statistical reporting should weigh relative to minor APA/statistical notation errors.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion clearly states the aim, answers the research question, and indicates which hypotheses were supported and which were not. The main conclusion is consistent with the reported results, and the student does engage with the unexpected finding that iVET did not outperform the waitlist. That is an important strength. The section also reconnects findings to earlier literature and theoretical mechanisms such as habituation and inhibitory learning, which shows good argumentative awareness. The practical implications for adolescent mental health care are also logically tied back to the societal relevance from the Introduction. At the same time, the interpretation is somewhat stronger than the study design and results warrant. The explanation for the weak iVET effect is plausible, but remains speculative because the study did not directly measure treatment burden, dropout tendencies, safety behavior, or learning processes. The limitations section is relevant, especially concerning comparability of scenarios and self-report measurement, though it could have addressed the absence of follow-up more prominently as a design limitation rather than only as a future direction. Overall, the Discussion is coherent, relevant, and above average for this level, though not fully comprehensive or consistently critical enough for a higher grade.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric usefully focuses on the reasoning toward the main conclusion and the relevance of the critical reflection. A possible improvement would be to make explicit that a strong discussion should interpret both expected and unexpected findings, reconnect to theory and prior literature, and distinguish between data-based conclusions and speculation. Those distinctions are important in this course and are described more clearly in the writing guide than in the rubric itself.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable, clearly structured, and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. Paragraphing is functional and the overall hourglass structure is recognizable. Most sections have a clear focus, and the argument is usually easy to follow. There are, however, several language and formatting issues that prevent a higher score. These include some awkward or repetitive phrasing, occasional grammar issues, inconsistent terminology, and multiple APA/reference inaccuracies. Examples include inconsistent year reporting, spelling mistakes in author names or article titles, punctuation issues, and some unclear formatting of tables. There are also small ambiguities in statistical notation and subsection transitions. Still, these problems do not seriously impede understanding. For this level, the writing is adequate to good, but not polished.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and practical, especially in distinguishing structure, grammar, APA, ambiguity, and redundancy. One limitation is that it may encourage assessors to merge quite different writing issues into one score without clear weighting. It could be improved by clarifying whether clarity and structure should count more heavily than minor APA issues, especially in a second-year methods course where scientific reasoning is the main learning objective.

intro_feedback: De introductie bevat een duidelijke en logisch opgebouwde aanleiding van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theoretisch kader, eerdere literatuur, kennislacune en uiteindelijk de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. Sterk is dat de tekst goed aansluit bij de doelgroep adolescenten en dat relevante mechanismen zoals vermijding, veiligheidsgedrag, habituatie en inhibitory learning worden gebruikt om VRET theoretisch te onderbouwen. Ook worden de verplichte kernstudies besproken en gekoppeld aan de eigen studie. De argumentatielijn is daardoor overwegend coherent en overtuigend. Wel zijn er enkele punten die de score beperken. De bespreking van eerdere studies blijft soms nog wat samenvattend in plaats van echt synthetiserend, en de stap van theorie naar de specifieke verwachting dat VRET effectiever zal zijn dan iVET had nog explicieter en scherper kunnen worden uitgewerkt. Daarnaast zit er enige onnauwkeurigheid in de literatuurverwijzingen, bijvoorbeeld Bouchard jaartal/positionering ten opzichte van de opgegeven kernliteratuur. Toch is dit voor dit niveau duidelijk bovengemiddeld.
intro_rubric_feedback: Het introductierubric maakt terecht onderscheid op de kwaliteit van de argumentatielijn richting onderzoeksvraag en hypothese. Een mogelijk verbeterpunt is dat de niveaus 'adequate', 'good' en 'excellent' sterk op elkaar lijken en vooral verschillen in mate van coherentie en overtuigingskracht, wat beoordelaars veel interpretatieruimte geeft. Meer concrete indicatoren, zoals expliciete aanwezigheid van maatschappelijke relevantie, theoretisch kader, synthese van literatuur en duidelijke overgang naar design/hypothese, zouden de toepasbaarheid vergroten.
methods_feedback: De methode is in de basis coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: een drie-groepen ontwerp met pre- en postmeting sluit aan bij de hypothesen. De participantenparagraaf bevat leeftijd, steekproefomvang en inclusie- en exclusiecriteria. Ook worden de behandelcondities inhoudelijk beschreven en is er aandacht voor random toewijzing. Dat maakt de methode overwegend begrijpelijk. De score wordt echter gedrukt doordat enkele essentiële onderdelen onvolledig of onduidelijk blijven. Zo ontbreken een heldere beschrijving van beloning/compensatie, de wijze van randomisatie, en belangrijke procedurele details zoals duur tussen pre- en postmeting. Bij de meetinstrumenten ontbreekt een volledig correcte en systematische beschrijving volgens de schrijfgids; er wordt bijvoorbeeld niet heel precies uitgewerkt hoe de totaalscore wordt berekend, en de gebruikte cut-off wordt genoemd zonder duidelijke verantwoording. Verder is er conceptuele onduidelijkheid rond de diagnostische procedure, onder meer door de formulering rond de SCID-5 en de verwijzing naar 'DSM-5 Childhood Disorders'. Replicatie is globaal mogelijk, maar niet sterk genoeg uitgewerkt voor een hogere score.
methods_rubric_feedback: Het methoderubric benoemt coherentie en volledigheid, maar blijft vrij globaal. Voor dit type opdracht zou het nuttig zijn om explicieter te specificeren welke minimale elementen aanwezig moeten zijn per subonderdeel, zoals inclusie/exclusie, randomisatie, allocatie, beloning, meetinstrumentdetails en procedurele timing. Dat zou beter aansluiten bij de schrijfgids en de betrouwbaarheid van beoordeling verhogen.
results_feedback: De resultaten bevatten de basisstructuur van een resultatensectie: er wordt iets gezegd over outliers en assumpties, er is een gekozen analyse, en de uitkomsten worden inhoudelijk geïnterpreteerd. Ook wordt geprobeerd tabellen en een figuur te gebruiken. Toch zijn er meerdere belangrijke problemen die maken dat deze sectie net voldoende is. Het grootste probleem is de inconsistentie en onjuistheid in de rapportage. De tekst verwijst naar Tabel 1, maar de tabellen zelf zijn rommelig weergegeven en de demografische tabel onderaan bevat een duidelijke foutieve of dubbele kolomindeling. Daarnaast klopt de inferentiële statistiek inhoudelijk niet goed met het beschreven design en de steekproef; bij een mixed ANOVA met 120 participanten en 2 meetmomenten zijn de gerapporteerde vrijheidsgraden van F(1, 357) en F(2, 357) niet plausibel. Ook is er een interne tegenspraak bij de post-hoc resultaten: er staat dat er bij prebehandeling geen significante verschillen zijn, terwijl p = .007 tweemaal juist wel significant zou zijn. Verder ontbreken de feitelijke tabellen in nette vorm in de sectie zelf, waardoor de lezer de analyse moeilijk kan controleren. De algemene richting van de resultaten is begrijpelijk, maar de statistische rapportage is te inconsistent voor een ruim voldoende.
results_rubric_feedback: Het resultatenrubric is bruikbaar in hoofdlijnen, maar de grens tussen 'mostly correct' en 'correct' blijft breed en lastig te operationaliseren. Zeker bij studentpapers zou het helpen als expliciet wordt genoemd dat correcte afstemming tussen design, analyse, vrijheidsgraden, tabellen en interpretatie zwaar meeweegt. Ook kan een verwijzing naar minimale vereisten, zoals descriptieve tabellen en begrijpelijke post-hocrapportage, de consistentie tussen beoordelaars vergroten.
discussion_feedback: De discussie begint sterk met een heldere terugkoppeling naar doel, onderzoeksvraag, hypothesen en de kernbevindingen. De student maakt duidelijk dat de hypothesen slechts gedeeltelijk zijn ondersteund en interpreteert de onverwachte afwezigheid van effect voor iVET in plaats van die te negeren. Dat is een belangrijk pluspunt. Ook worden de bevindingen teruggekoppeld aan eerder onderzoek en aan de theoretische mechanismen van habituatie en inhibitory learning. Verder bevat de discussie relevante beperkingen en redelijke suggesties voor toekomstig onderzoek, plus een terugkeer naar de maatschappelijke relevantie. De score blijft iets onder echt hoog niveau omdat de discussie op sommige punten nog wat eenzijdig redeneert in de richting van de eigen verwachting. De alternatieve verklaringen voor het uitblijven van iVET-effecten hadden kritischer en specifieker uitgewerkt kunnen worden, bijvoorbeeld in relatie tot designkeuzes, meetmomenten, implementatie of statistische onzekerheid. Ook worden de beperkingen deels goed genoemd, maar niet volledig verbonden aan wat dit betekent voor de sterkte van de conclusies. Al met al wel een goede, samenhangende discussie voor dit niveau.
discussion_rubric_feedback: Het discussierubric legt terecht nadruk op redenering, conclusie en kritische reflectie. Een mogelijke aanscherping is om expliciet op te nemen dat onverwachte of niet-ondersteunende bevindingen inhoudelijk moeten worden besproken, omdat dit in wetenschappelijke redeneervaardigheid een belangrijk onderscheid maakt tussen gemiddelde en sterke papers. Ook zou een explicieter criterium over terugkoppeling naar theorie en eerdere literatuur de rubric nog functioneler maken.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar, academisch van toon en logisch opgebouwd. De meeste paragrafen hebben een duidelijk focuspunt en de lijn van het betoog is meestal goed te volgen. Voor een tweedejaarsstudent is de schrijfstijl overwegend degelijk. Er zijn echter meerdere taal- en APA-onzorgvuldigheden die een hogere score in de weg staan. Voorbeelden zijn inconsistenties in referenties, enkele typefouten en slordigheden in namen en jaartallen, onhandige formuleringen, en zichtbare problemen in de opmaak van tabellen. Ook is er soms herhaling in de uitleg van theorie. De taal belemmert het begrip niet ernstig, maar de afwerking is niet strak genoeg voor een hogere beoordeling.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: Het taal- en stijlrubric is relatief duidelijk, maar combineert veel verschillende aspecten in één criterium: taal, structuur, APA, vaagheid en redundantie. Daardoor kan onduidelijk worden welk type fout zwaarder moet wegen. Een opsplitsing of een korte toelichting over de relatieve weging van begrijpelijkheid versus formele APA-precisie zou de beoordelingsconsistentie verbeteren, zeker bij papers van beginnende studenten.

intro_feedback: De introductie bevat een duidelijke en logische opbouw van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theoretisch kader, eerdere literatuur, kennislacune, onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. Positief is dat kernbegrippen zoals vermijdingsgedrag, veiligheidsgedrag, habituatie en inhibitory learning worden uitgelegd en functioneel worden gekoppeld aan exposuretherapie en VRET. Ook worden de verplichte kernstudies besproken en wordt de relevantie van adolescenten als doelgroep goed onderbouwd. De onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen zijn helder en sluiten aan bij de voorafgaande argumentatie. Wel blijft de synthese soms nog wat beschrijvend: de studies worden vooral na elkaar besproken in plaats van sterk geïntegreerd als bouwstenen in één doorlopende redenering. Daarnaast is de onderbouwing voor de verwachting dat VRET effectiever zal zijn dan iVET sterker voor acceptatie/toegankelijkheid dan voor daadwerkelijke symptoomreductie, waardoor dat deel van de argumentatie iets minder overtuigend is. Ook zijn er enkele onnauwkeurigheden in de literatuurverwijzingen, zoals Bouchard et al. (2016/2017). Binnen het niveau van tweedejaarsstudenten is dit echter een bovengemiddeld sterke introductie.
intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is bruikbaar omdat zij de kern legt bij line of reasoning, relevantie, hypothese en verantwoord brongebruik. Wel zou de rubric nog duidelijker kunnen onderscheiden tussen een tekst die vooral beschrijvend literatuur samenvat en een tekst die studies echt synthetiseert tot een overtuigend argument. Zeker voor dit vak is dat verschil belangrijk. Ook kan explicieter worden gemaakt hoe maatschappelijke relevantie en theoretische relevantie zich tot elkaar verhouden binnen de beoordeling.
methods_feedback: De methode is in grote lijnen coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: een vergelijking tussen VRET, iVET en wachtlijst met pre- en postmeting. De onderdelen participanten, materialen en procedure zijn aanwezig, en de beschrijving van de VRET-conditie is relatief concreet. Ook zijn inclusie- en exclusiecriteria genoemd. Toch zijn er meerdere onvolledigheden die de repliceerbaarheid beperken. Zo ontbreekt een duidelijke beschrijving van de randomisatieprocedure, wordt niet uitgelegd hoe de SCID-5 Junior precies is afgenomen, en ontbreken belangrijke vereiste participantgegevens zoals beloning/compensatie. De iVET-conditie is merkbaar minder precies uitgewerkt dan de VRET-conditie, waardoor de vergelijkbaarheid tussen condities onvoldoende transparant is. Verder staat procedurele informatie deels onder Materialen, en ontbreken details over timing van de postmeting en praktische uitvoering van de sessies. Er is dus sprake van een samenhangende maar slechts gedeeltelijk volledig uitgewerkte methode.
methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek benoemt terecht coherentie met RQ en volledigheid van participanten, materialen en procedure, maar blijft relatief globaal. Voor dit type opdracht zou het helpen om explicieter te benoemen welke minimale elementen verwacht worden, zoals randomisatie, inclusie/exclusie, groepsindeling, meetmomenten, beloning en voldoende detail over interventies en meetinstrumenten. Het grootste probleem is de interne inconsistentie van de gerapporteerde tabellen en tekst: Tabel 1 en Tabel 2 zijn niet netjes geïntegreerd in de sectie, en onderaan het document lijken losse of dubbel opgenomen tabellen te staan. In Tabel 1 lijkt bovendien een extra iVET-kolom te zijn toegevoegd, wat wijst op een opmaak- of constructiefout. In de tekst staat verder dat er bij prebehandeling geen significante verschillen zijn, maar vervolgens worden p-waarden van .007 gerapporteerd voor twee vergelijkingen, wat in tegenspraak is met die conclusie. Daarnaast zijn er statistische rapportagefouten, zoals vrijheidsgraden die niet goed lijken te passen bij een mixed ANOVA met 120 participanten en formuleringen als 'p =< .001'. Ook ontbreken de feitelijke tabellen en figuur op een correcte, leesbare manier in de resultatensectie zelf. De algemene analysekeuze past wel bij het design, maar de rapportage is te inconsistent om sterker beoordeeld te worden.

intro_feedback: De introductie heeft een duidelijke en grotendeels coherente opbouw van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theorie, eerdere literatuur, onderzoeksgat en hypothesen. Wat de score iets beperkt, is dat de literatuurintegratie niet overal even sterk is: sommige studies worden nog vrij sequentieel samengevat in plaats van echt systematisch tegen elkaar afgezet.
