A useful refinement would be to make explicit that strong discussions should not only restate findings but also interpret unexpected results, connect back to theory from the Introduction, and avoid overstating implications relative to the design. These expectations are present in the writing guide and calibration notes, but incorporating them more directly into the rubric would improve consistency across graders.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the scientific register is mostly appropriate. The structure of the major sections is clear, and the reader can usually follow the argument without difficulty. Paragraphs mostly have a clear focus, and transitions are often functional. However, there are noticeable language and style issues that keep this below average-to-adequate polish. There are repeated grammar and phrasing problems, awkward wording, spacing and punctuation inconsistencies, capitalization inconsistencies, and several APA/reference errors. Some sentences are overly long or imprecise, and terminology is not always used consistently (for example, varying labels for conditions and some citation/year inconsistencies). The formatting of the Results table and reference list also weakens presentation substantially. These issues do not seriously impede understanding, but they are frequent enough to lower the style score.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and useful, especially in separating clarity, structure, grammar, APA, vagueness, and redundancy. One possible improvement is to clarify how much formatting issues in tables, headings, and references should weigh relative to sentence-level language problems. At present, many different dimensions are combined, which can make it hard to decide between adjacent categories. More explicit anchoring to student-level expectations could also help graders avoid over-penalizing minor APA issues in otherwise clear papers.

intro_feedback: The Introduction presents a clear topic, establishes societal relevance, and leads to a clear research aim and hypothesis. The overall line of reasoning is mostly sound: SAD is important, exposure-based approaches are relevant, VRET appears promising, and self-guided VRET may reduce barriers further. The paper also includes the required core studies plus an additional study. This places the section solidly in the adequate range. The main weakness is synthesis. Much of the literature review is still study-by-study summary rather than consistently using the studies as building blocks in one argument. The theoretical framework is also somewhat underdeveloped: exposure theory is mentioned, but the paper does not fully build a clear theory explaining why therapist guidance should improve outcomes over self-guidance, especially over time. In addition, there are some inaccuracies or inconsistencies relative to the course materials (e.g., years/authors for core studies, and the hypothesis only explicitly mentions post-treatment despite the design including follow-up). These issues weaken coherence somewhat, but the introduction still justifies the RQ reasonably well.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is generally clear and appropriately emphasizes argumentative coherence, use of theory, synthesis of prior research, and the link to the RQ and hypotheses. A useful improvement would be to operationalize what counts as a 'major component' from the writing guide more explicitly, because graders may differ in how strongly they weigh societal relevance, theory, transition to design, and inclusion of all core studies. The wording around 'at least 60%' or '80% of the conclusions are convincing' is also hard to apply consistently; more concrete indicators would improve reliability. It may also help to specify how to handle papers that include all required studies but discuss them mainly descriptively.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and aligned with the stated research question and hypothesis. The participant section includes key details such as sample size, age, gender, inclusion/exclusion criteria, random assignment, and compensation. The general design is understandable and mostly replicable for this student level. Materials and procedure are also mostly complete, and the distinction between the two conditions is described clearly enough. This supports an adequate grade. The main limitations are missing or underdeveloped details that matter for replication: the diagnosis procedure is named but not described further; inclusion criteria beyond SAD diagnosis are minimal; the intervention protocol is still somewhat vague; and the timing/context of some assessments could be specified more precisely. In the Materials section, the questionnaire description is reasonably complete, but developer information is not introduced in the recommended way and the intervention description remains relatively broad. There is also some procedural content mixed into Materials and some wording that could be more precise. Still, the section is coherent and mostly complete rather than conceptually flawed.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is practical and well aligned with the writing guide, especially its focus on coherence, completeness, and placement of information. One area for refinement is the distinction between the adequate and good bands: the difference between 'lack one or two important details' and 'complete and correct, but may have unnecessary details' can be subtle in practice. The rubric could benefit from naming a few anchor details that are especially important at this level, such as allocation procedure, assessment timing, condition differences, and sufficient instrument description. That would improve inter-rater consistency.
results_feedback: The Results section reports the main analysis in a way that is broadly aligned with the stated design: descriptive statistics are provided, a mixed ANOVA is reported, assumptions are discussed, and post-hoc comparisons are included. This is enough to keep the section in the adequate range. However, compared with the sample structure, the section is notably incomplete and somewhat poorly presented. The descriptive table is malformed and difficult to read, the demographics table is missing from the Results section, and there is no figure. The results mention assumption checks and outliers, but these are not reported with much precision. The reporting of the statistical outcomes is mostly understandable, but not as complete or polished as expected from the sample. The interpretation of the interaction and follow-up comparisons is clear, which helps, but the missing structural elements prevent a higher score.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is helpful because it anchors expectations to the sample results section and makes clear that completeness and correspondence to design matter most. A possible improvement would be to separate 'content completeness' from 'presentation quality' more explicitly. For example, missing a figure, malformed tables, or missing demographics in Results can all reduce quality, but the current wording leaves some ambiguity about how much each should matter. Clearer anchors for what constitutes roughly average performance relative to the sample would support more consistent grading.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion clearly states the main conclusion, answers the research question, and addresses both the immediate post-treatment difference and the convergence at follow-up. It links findings back to earlier literature and offers several study-specific limitations, which is a strength. The unexpected follow-up improvement in the self-guided group is not ignored, and the student attempts to explain it, which is important and appropriate for this assignment. These features support a solid adequate score. The main reason the section does not move into the good range is that some interpretation remains somewhat speculative and not fully anchored in the theoretical framework introduced earlier. The discussion connects to previous studies, but often at a general level rather than deeply integrating theory and evidence. Some implications are a bit stronger than the data warrant, especially given the design differences between conditions that the student later acknowledges as limitations. Overall, though, the reasoning is mostly coherent, study-specific, and meaningful.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately prioritizes conclusion quality, linkage to introduction/theory, interpretation relative to previous research, and study-specific limitations. This is well suited to the course goals. One improvement would be to distinguish more clearly between merely mentioning theory and actually using theory to interpret results. Another helpful refinement would be to clarify how to weigh speculative explanations for unexpected findings: some speculation is pedagogically appropriate, but the rubric could say more explicitly that higher bands require such interpretations to be clearly framed as tentative and grounded in evidence.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the scientific tone is mostly appropriate. Section structure is clear, terminology is mostly understandable, and the intended argument can be followed throughout. This supports a passing score in the adequate/developing boundary area. The main issue is the number of writing, formatting, and APA-related inconsistencies. There are repeated spacing and punctuation errors, inconsistent terms such as 'selfguided', 'self-guided', and 'Therapistguided', several awkward sentences, and multiple APA/reference inaccuracies. The Results table formatting is especially problematic and disrupts presentation quality. These issues do not usually obscure meaning, so they should not heavily lower the scientific reasoning grades, but they do justify a somewhat lower Language & Style score.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and useful, especially because it prevents language issues from unfairly lowering scientific reasoning scores. However, the error-count approach may be difficult to apply consistently across papers of different lengths. It may help to complement the counts with more functional criteria, such as how often language problems interrupt comprehension or weaken academic tone. The distinction between adequate and good is otherwise sensible, but APA, grammar, and clarity could perhaps be weighted more explicitly within this rubric to support more reliable scoring.

intro_feedback: The Introduction presents a clear research topic, establishes societal relevance early, and ends with a specific comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET. The research question and hypothesis are understandable and the general line of reasoning is mostly coherent. The student also includes the required core VRET studies and an additional article relevant to self-guided VRET. A strength is that prior studies are used to justify why comparing guided versus self-guided VRET matters. However, the argumentation is more often sequential summary than true synthesis. The theoretical framework is relatively limited: exposure/extinction is explained, but the theory is not fully developed to account for why therapist guidance should alter outcomes, especially over time. Some claims are asserted too strongly or somewhat vaguely, and there are factual/reference inconsistencies with the required core-study years. The long-term design is mentioned, but the rationale for expecting follow-up differences is underdeveloped. Overall, this fits the adequate range: sound and mostly coherent, with some building-block reasoning, but not yet consistently well synthesized.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing line of reasoning, synthesis, and the role of prior research in leading to the RQ. One area to refine is that it bundles many different requirements together, which can make borderline cases hard to score consistently. It may help to separate 'presence of required components' from 'quality of synthesis/argumentation' more explicitly. The criterion about recent references is useful, but could clarify how to treat classic theoretical sources that are older than 25 years yet still legitimate.
methods_feedback: The Methods section describes a coherent study that matches the stated aim and hypothesis. Participants, allocation, exclusion criteria, intervention structure, and the main outcome measure are all included. The LSAS-SR is described with item count, response scale, score range, and an example, which aligns well with the guide. The procedure is mostly chronological and understandable. The section is weakened by some missing or insufficiently precise details that matter for replication: inclusion criteria beyond DSM-5 diagnosis are limited, the exact treatment protocol is not described in enough depth, and the analysis plan is missing as a separate element. There is also some imbalance in condition setup that raises design concerns, such as differences in location and instruction format, although the student later reflects on this in the Discussion. Some phrasing in Materials is somewhat procedural, and certain intervention details remain vague, especially how the virtual therapist functioned and what was standardized between conditions. Still, the study design is coherent and mostly complete for this level, so an adequate grade is appropriate.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately focuses on coherence with the RQ and on completeness relative to the writing guide. A useful improvement would be to distinguish more clearly between missing minor reporting details and design features that threaten interpretability, because both currently sit under similar wording. It could also explicitly mention the analysis subsection, since students are often unsure whether statistical plans belong in Methods and this matters for alignment with Results.
results_feedback: The Results section includes the main statistical test appropriate to the design, reports main effects and the interaction with degrees of freedom and p-values, and describes post-hoc comparisons in a generally understandable way. This shows that the student understands the broad structure expected for a mixed ANOVA write-up. However, the section is clearly incomplete relative to the sample and rubric expectations. The descriptive table is malformed and not properly presented; the demographic table is missing; means are not clearly shown in a readable final format; and there is no figure. Assumption checks are described only in broad terms without supporting statistics. Reporting is also somewhat inconsistent: the text says there were no invalid data, but later mentions outliers; wording such as 'the research has decided' is not appropriate scientific reporting style. The section remains interpretable and broadly relevant to the stated design, but because multiple expected reporting elements are missing or poorly formatted, it falls in the developing range rather than adequate.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric gives helpful anchoring through the sample section and appropriately emphasizes completeness and relevance to the design. A useful refinement would be to define more explicitly how heavily to weigh missing formatting elements such as tables and figures versus reasonably correct narrative reporting. At present, a paper with correct inferential logic but missing one or two structural elements may be hard to place consistently between developing and adequate.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion clearly restates the aim, answers the research question, and links the main findings back to the hypothesis. The student does more than simply repeat results; they interpret the pattern that therapist-guided VRET had stronger short-term effects while self-guided VRET appeared to catch up by follow-up. The discussion also makes meaningful links to previous literature, especially the earlier VRET studies and the self-guided study by Zainal et al. A notable strength is that the student engages with the unexpected continued improvement in the self-guided condition instead of ignoring it. Several limitations are specific to the study, including context differences between conditions, generalizability, and confounding of treatment setting. These are relevant and reasonably argued. The weaker aspects are that the theoretical integration is only moderate: the discussion introduces self-efficacy as an explanation, but that theory was not really developed in the Introduction, and the implications for the original framework are therefore not fully worked through. Some conclusions are a little stronger than the design warrants. Overall, though, the reasoning is mostly correct, coherent, and study-specific, fitting the adequate range.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric rightly emphasizes interpretation, linkage to theory, prior research, and study-specific critical reflection. It could be improved by distinguishing more explicitly between merely naming limitations and actually explaining their likely consequences for interpretation. It may also help to specify how to judge cases where students bring in a plausible new theory in the Discussion that was not sufficiently established in the Introduction.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. Sectioning is clear and the reader can usually follow the argument. Terminology is mostly consistent, and the paper has a recognizable academic structure. However, there are enough language and formatting issues to keep this from the good range. There are multiple grammar and punctuation problems, awkward phrasings, spacing inconsistencies, and citation/reference inconsistencies. APA style has several errors, including inconsistent years for key references, formatting problems in the reference list, and table presentation issues. There are also some ambiguous or imprecise formulations, especially in the Results and some theoretical claims. These problems do not usually block understanding, but they are noticeable throughout. That places the paper around satisfactory to adequate for Language & Style.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is comprehensive and useful, especially in preventing over-penalizing content grades for writing issues. However, some criteria depend on counting errors, which may reduce inter-rater consistency because assessors may count differently. It may help to give anchors with examples of what counts as a distinct grammar, APA, or ambiguity error. The rubric could also more clearly separate surface-level APA issues from deeper clarity and structure issues, since those do not affect readability equally.

intro_feedback: The Introduction presents a clear research topic, gives societal relevance early, includes the required core studies plus an additional relevant study, and ends with a clear research aim and hypothesis. The overall line of reasoning is mostly coherent: SAD is important, exposure is effective but burdensome, VRET may reduce barriers, and self-guided VRET could further improve accessibility. That said, the argumentation is more adequate than strong. Much of the previous research is handled study-by-study rather than fully synthesized as building blocks. The theoretical framework is present in a basic way through exposure/extinction logic, but it is not developed enough to clearly explain why therapist guidance should outperform self-guidance, especially over time. Some claims are too strong or insufficiently supported, and there are several small inaccuracies or inconsistencies in the cited core studies and terminology. The final design description is clear, but the hypothesis only addresses post-treatment while the introduction also motivates follow-up effects; that makes the logic slightly incomplete. Overall, the section fits the adequate band: sound and mostly coherent, with some synthesis and a justified RQ, but not consistently strong enough for the good band.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing coherence, synthesis, and the role of prior research in building toward the RQ. A useful refinement would be to make the expected role of theory even more explicit, since students can currently meet much of the rubric through empirical summary with only a minimal theoretical framework. It may also help to distinguish more clearly between 'all components present' and 'components used argumentatively,' because those are conceptually different skills. Finally, the rubric could clarify how to handle minor inaccuracies in referencing required core studies when the overall argumentative line remains sound.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and aligned with the stated research question and hypothesis. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the reader can broadly understand how the study would be conducted. Important required details are included, such as diagnostic inclusion, exclusion criteria, random assignment, compensation, sample demographics, intervention schedule, and the main outcome measure. The LSAS-SR is described at a reasonable student level with items, scale, scoring, and a validity reference. However, there are still one to two notable weaknesses that keep the section from the good band. The Materials description mixes intervention content with procedural information, and the self-guided and therapist-guided conditions are not specified in enough detail for strong replicability. For instance, the exact content of sessions, how the virtual therapist operates, and what was standardized across conditions remain somewhat vague. There is also no separate analysis subsection, despite the guide indicating analyses as part of Methods-level completeness. Still, the design is coherent, largely complete, and understandable for this course level.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately focuses on coherence, completeness, and correct placement of information. A possible improvement would be to specify more concretely what counts as 'important details' for this assignment, such as allocation, timing, operationalization of conditions, and measurement administration. This would improve reliability between graders. The rubric might also mention the analysis plan explicitly, since that is often part of methodological completeness in student papers but is not currently foregrounded in the performance bands.
results_feedback: The Results section reports the main mixed ANOVA appropriately for the design and includes interpretation of main effects and the interaction. The section also addresses assumptions and reports post-hoc comparisons in a way that is broadly understandable. This shows a mostly correct and relevant analysis structure. However, the section is weaker than the sample-based expectation for an average-to-good result. The main problem is incompleteness and presentation quality. The demographic table is missing, and the outcome table is malformed and placed partly outside the table itself. The section refers to a table 'below' but the formatting is disorganized, making it harder to follow. A figure is also missing, even though the sample strongly indicates that a graphical presentation should be included. Assumption checks are stated but not actually reported in detail, and some wording is informal or imprecise. Because the statistical test choice and the main conclusions are still coherent and mostly correct, this fits the adequate band rather than developing, but it falls below a strong average result.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is helpful because it anchors expectations to the sample and explicitly notes the required elements. That said, it could be improved by distinguishing more clearly between statistical correctness and presentation completeness. At present, a paper with the right analysis but missing tables/figure can be hard to place precisely. It may also help to specify whether detailed assumption statistics are expected or whether brief assumption statements are sufficient at this course level, since this is a common source of grading inconsistency.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion clearly restates the aim, answers the research question, and interprets the main findings in relation to the hypothesis. It does more than simply repeat the results: it identifies the immediate superiority of therapist-guided VRET and the convergence at follow-up, and it attempts to explain both patterns. The section also links back to prior literature and includes several study-specific limitations, especially concerning measurement context and treatment context. This is a meaningful strength. Still, the discussion remains mostly adequate rather than good. The theoretical integration is only partial: the discussion mentions human support and self-efficacy, but it does not clearly return to a well-developed theoretical framework from the introduction, nor does it systematically evaluate what the findings imply for that framework. Comparison with earlier studies is present but somewhat broad and not always very analytical. Some interpretations are plausible but speculative, particularly the self-efficacy explanation, and these are not strongly weighed against alternatives. Broader societal implications are mentioned in the conclusion, but they are not fully developed in a nuanced way. Overall, the reasoning is correct and mostly complete, with relevant limitations and literature links, which supports an adequate grade.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the most important dimensions well: conclusion quality, interpretation, linkage to introduction/theory, and critical reflection. A useful refinement would be to separate 'connection to theory' from 'comparison to prior research' more explicitly, because students may do one better than the other. The rubric could also give more guidance on how to weigh plausible but speculative explanations of unexpected findings, which are common in this assignment type and can vary widely in quality.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally readable and the overall structure is clear, with recognizable sections and a mostly scientific tone. Terminology is usually understandable, and the argument can be followed without major confusion. However, there are enough language, style, formatting, and APA issues to keep this in the adequate-to-developing range rather than clearly satisfactory. There are repeated spacing and punctuation errors, inconsistent hyphenation and capitalization (for example around self-guided/therapist-guided labels), awkward phrasing, and several citation/reference inaccuracies. Some sentences are overly long or unpolished, and there is occasional redundancy. APA issues are visible in both in-text citations and the reference list. Importantly, these problems usually do not block comprehension, so they should not strongly affect the scientific reasoning grades, but they do justify a somewhat lower Language & Style score.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is appropriately designed to prevent language issues from dominating content grades. Its criteria are clear overall, but some thresholds are very count-based, especially for grammar and APA errors, which may reduce consistency because not all errors are equally serious. It might be more useful to distinguish between errors that merely affect polish and errors that affect readability or professionalism. The rubric could also clarify how heavily formatting issues in tables and references should weigh relative to sentence-level writing quality.

intro_feedback: De introductie heeft een duidelijke en overwegend sterke argumentatielijn van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theorie, eerder onderzoek, kennislacune en onderzoeksvraag. De maatschappelijke relevantie wordt vroeg en concreet uitgewerkt, en de theoretische bespreking van vermijding, inhibitory learning en expectancy violation sluit goed aan op het onderwerp. Ook worden de verplichte kernstudies functioneel ingezet om de keuze voor VRET te onderbouwen. Sterk is bovendien dat de student een specifieke lacune formuleert, namelijk de rol van begeleiding binnen VRET. Wel zijn er enkele punten die de overtuigingskracht iets beperken. De introductie is vrij lang en bevat op sommige plekken herhaling, waardoor de lijn minder scherp wordt dan mogelijk was. De koppeling tussen zelfdeterminatietheorie/autonomie en de uiteindelijke hypothesen is interessant, maar blijft wat speculatief en wordt empirisch minder sterk onderbouwd dan de rest. Daarnaast had de overgang naar het concrete design nog compacter en explicieter gekund, bijvoorbeeld door scherper te benoemen waarom precies deze drie condities nodig zijn. Al met al is dit een bovengemiddelde introductie: coherent, relevant en redelijk overtuigend, maar nog niet overal even strak of volledig uitgewerkt.
intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek legt terecht de nadruk op de redeneringslijn naar onderzoeksvraag, relevantie en hypothese. Een mogelijke verbetering is om explicieter te onderscheiden tussen 'coherent', 'convincing' en 'very convincing', omdat die niveaus nu interpretatieruimte laten. Ook zou de rubric nog specifieker kunnen benoemen dat literatuursynthese zwaarder weegt dan losse samenvatting van studies, aangezien dat in deze cursus een kernvaardigheid is.
methods_feedback: De methodesectie beschrijft een coherent design dat duidelijk aansluit op de onderzoeksvraag en hypothesen. De participanten, globale inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, randomisatie en de drie condities worden begrijpelijk weergegeven. Ook is positief dat de student probeert verschillen tussen condities te standaardiseren en dat de keuze voor het aantal sessies inhoudelijk wordt onderbouwd. Tegelijkertijd blijft de methode op meerdere punten te globaal voor een echt sterke score. Belangrijke onderdelen ontbreken of zijn onvoldoende precies uitgewerkt, zoals een demografische beschrijving van de uiteindelijke steekproef (gemiddelde leeftijd, SD, genderverdeling), informatie over eventuele vergoeding, en een concretere operationalisatie van hoe de SAD-diagnose is vastgesteld. De beschrijving van de materialen is beperkt tot de LSAS-SR en mist onderdelen uit de schrijfgids, zoals ontwikkelaar van de self-reportversie, voorbeelditem en meer precieze informatie over scoring/cut-offs. Ook zijn de interventies nog tamelijk algemeen beschreven: er is te weinig detail over de exacte taken, verschillen tussen condities, en hoe vergelijkbaarheid tussen VR en in vivo praktisch wordt gewaarborgd. Daarnaast staan ontwerp- en rechtvaardigingselementen deels onder Materialen/Interventies in plaats van strak gescheiden in Materials en Procedure. Daarmee is de methode adequaat en voldoende samenhangend, maar nog niet compleet of precies genoeg voor een hogere beoordeling.
methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek is bruikbaar doordat zij nadruk legt op samenhang tussen design, onderzoeksvraag en beschrijving van participanten, materialen en procedure. Wel zou de rubric sterker worden als explicieter wordt opgenomen welke minimale elementen verwacht worden voor voldoende/goed, zoals toewijzing aan condities, inclusie/exclusie, demografische kenmerken, operationalisaties en voldoende detail voor repliceerbaarheid op studentniveau. Dat zou de beoordeling consistenter maken.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie laat zien dat de student de juiste analyse heeft gekozen passend bij het 3 x 2 mixed design, en de tekst is in grote lijnen begrijpelijk. Positief is dat assumpties worden genoemd, dat hoofd- en interactie-effecten worden gerapporteerd en dat de conclusies aansluiten op de gerapporteerde uitkomsten. Ook worden post-hocvergelijkingen kort besproken. Toch schiet deze sectie duidelijk tekort ten opzichte van de verwachtingen uit de voorbeeldresultaten en rubric. Er ontbreekt een demografische tabel volledig. Daarnaast is Tabel 1 in de resultaten zelf niet daadwerkelijk uitgewerkt in conventionele vorm, en Figuur 1 wordt genoemd maar niet gerapporteerd of toegelicht op het niveau dat verwacht wordt. De integratie van de tabel aan het einde van het document maakt de presentatie bovendien rommelig en minder coherent. Verder zijn er enkele inhoudelijke/statistische onduidelijkheden: een partial eta squared van .53 bij F(1,117)=688.45 lijkt niet plausibel en roept twijfel op over de correctheid van de effectgrootte; ook zijn de post-hocanalyses bij een niet-significante interactie niet goed gemotiveerd. Voor dit niveau hoeven resultaten niet perfect te zijn, maar vergeleken met het sample-document is de rapportage onvolledig en minder zorgvuldig uitgewerkt. Daarom is dit net onder gemiddeld.
results_rubric_feedback: De resultatenrubriek benoemt correctheid, volledigheid, coherentie en relevantie, maar blijft relatief globaal. Omdat er ook een voorbeeldresultatensectie is, zou het helpen als de rubric explicieter verwijst naar verplichte onderdelen zoals een demografietabel, descriptieve statistieken per conditie en meetmoment, assumptiechecks en passende follow-up/post-hocanalyses. Dat maakt de vertaalslag van rubric naar concrete beoordeling transparanter.
discussion_feedback: De discussie heeft een duidelijke hoofdconclusie en beantwoordt de onderzoeksvraag expliciet. De student bespreekt correct dat alle interventies tot afname in sociale angst leidden en dat de hypothese over superioriteit van begeleide interventies niet werd ondersteund. Ook is sterk dat de bevindingen worden teruggekoppeld aan de literatuur en aan het inhibitory learning-kader. De student probeert bovendien alternatieve verklaringen te geven voor het uitblijven van groepsverschillen, wat getuigt van wetenschappelijke reflectie. De beperkingen en suggesties voor vervolgonderzoek zijn relevant en grotendeels studiespecifiek, zoals het ontbreken van follow-up en procesmaten. Wat de score iets drukt, is dat een deel van de discussie vrij dicht blijft bij de introductie en soms meer theoretisch plausibel redeneert dan echt vanuit de concrete dataset. De implicaties voor theorie zijn aanwezig, maar hadden nog explicieter kunnen aangeven welk onderdeel van het theoretisch model nu wel en niet getest is. Ook zijn de bredere maatschappelijke implicaties slechts beperkt uitgewerkt in relatie tot de openingsparagrafen over toegankelijkheid en druk op de zorg. Verder staat er een duidelijke doublure in de eerste alinea. Desondanks is de redenering coherent en inhoudelijk degelijk, dus dit is een bovengemiddelde discussie.
discussion_rubric_feedback: De discussierubriek past goed bij het cursusdoel doordat zij nadruk legt op de redenering naar de conclusie en kritische reflectie. Een nuttige aanscherping zou zijn om expliciet te benoemen dat een goede discussie niet alleen resultaten moet herhalen, maar deze ook moet interpreteren in relatie tot verwachting, theorie, alternatieve verklaringen en maatschappelijke implicaties. Vooral het onderscheid tussen 'relevant' en 'convincingly argued' kan nog concreter geoperationaliseerd worden.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen helder, goed leesbaar en voldoende wetenschappelijk van toon. De opbouw van de paper is logisch en de meeste paragrafen hebben een herkenbare focus. Verwijzingen worden meestal verantwoord gebruikt en de formuleringen zijn doorgaans precies genoeg voor dit niveau. Er zijn echter wel meerdere kleine stilistische en formele problemen die een hogere score in de weg staan. Zo komt er herhaling voor, onder andere in de discussie waar een zin dubbel staat. Ook is de resultatenpresentatie qua vormgeving onhandig geïntegreerd, wat de professionele indruk vermindert. Daarnaast zijn er enkele APA- en referentieonvolkomenheden, zoals inconsistenties in kapitalisatie, auteursnotatie en bronvermelding. Sommige zinnen zijn vrij lang en hadden compacter gekund om de argumentatie scherper te maken. Dit alles past bij degelijk, bovengemiddeld schrijfwerk van een tweedejaarsstudent, maar nog niet bij echt sterk afgewerkt taal- en stijlgebruik.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: De rubric voor taal en stijl is redelijk volledig en passend voor dit niveau, omdat ze zowel helderheid, structuur als APA meeneemt. Wel combineert zij veel verschillende dimensies in één criterium, waardoor het soms lastig is om precies te bepalen waarom een paper op een bepaald niveau uitkomt. Een opsplitsing of nadere concretisering van de weging van structuur, taalcorrectheid en APA zou de betrouwbaarheid van beoordeling kunnen vergroten.

intro_feedback: The introduction shows a clear and generally convincing line of reasoning toward the research question. It starts with societal relevance, explains SAD well, links avoidance and inhibitory learning to exposure, and then narrows logically to VRET and the specific gap regarding self-guided versus therapist-guided VRET. The research question is clear and relevant, and the hypotheses follow from the preceding argument. The literature is mostly used responsibly and the required core studies are included. Strong points are the explicit theoretical framing and the clear justification of why comparing guidance levels within VRET matters scientifically and societally. The main weaknesses are that some parts are somewhat lengthy and repetitive, and the literature integration is still a bit more summary-like than fully synthetic in places. In addition, some theoretical elements, such as autonomy and control, are introduced somewhat broadly and could have been linked more tightly to the exact hypothesis. Overall, this is above-average for this course level and fits the 'good' range rather than 'excellent'.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the importance of coherence, relevance, and responsible reference use well, but it could distinguish more explicitly between mere summary of literature and actual synthesis/building-block reasoning. At present, papers with a clear topic and acceptable RQ may score similarly to papers with a genuinely strong argumentative line. Adding descriptors about integration of theory and prior studies, and about how explicitly the hypotheses are derived from that reasoning, would improve discrimination between adequate, good, and excellent performances.
methods_feedback: The methods section describes a coherent design that matches the research question and hypotheses. The participant section includes sample size, age range, recruitment, inclusion and exclusion criteria, and random allocation. The intervention conditions are clearly distinguished, and the overall mixed design is stated explicitly. This makes the study understandable at a general level. However, the section is only moderately complete relative to the writing guide. Important required details are missing, such as mean age, standard deviation, gender distribution, compensation or reward, and more precise implementation details for the interventions. The materials section is also limited: only one measure is described, and although the LSAS-SR is explained reasonably well, the developer/reference is not fully aligned with the writing guide expectations. Some content that belongs more naturally in Procedure or Design is placed under Materials/Interventions. Procedure is understandable, but it remains fairly brief and does not provide enough detail to make replication easy, especially for timing, setting, and session execution. So the section is coherent and mostly correct, but not fully complete.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately emphasizes coherence with the RQ and completeness of participants, materials, and procedure. However, the categories could be made more concrete by explicitly naming expected details such as allocation, inclusion/exclusion justification, demographics, compensation, and enough procedural detail for replication at student level. This would help distinguish between 'nearly complete' and 'complete' more consistently across graders.
results_feedback: The results section reports the main analysis in a structure that is generally appropriate for this course level: descriptive means are provided, assumptions are addressed, the mixed ANOVA is stated, and the main effects and interaction are reported in a readable way. The interpretation of the statistical pattern is also correct and consistent with the stated design. However, the section falls below the sample-based expectation for an average-to-good Results section because it is incomplete in important ways. The demographics table is missing, and Table 1 is referred to in the text but not properly presented as a formatted table within the section itself. Figure 1 is mentioned but not actually shown. The reporting of assumption checks is acceptable, but the section is less complete and transparent than the sample template suggests. There is also a notable statistical inconsistency: the reported partial eta squared for a very large F-value appears implausible, which raises concern about reporting accuracy. Minor APA/statistical issues alone would not lower the grade much, but the missing required elements and possible reporting inconsistency justify a somewhat below-average section score.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is useful in focusing on correctness, completeness, coherence, and relevance, but it remains somewhat broad. Given the course calibration and sample results, it would help to embed expected student-level anchors such as presence of demographic and descriptive tables, reporting of assumptions, appropriate main analysis, and post-hoc tests where relevant. That would make grading more transparent and better aligned with the provided sample.
discussion_feedback: The discussion gives a clear main conclusion and answers the research question directly. It correctly states that all interventions reduced social anxiety and that the expected superiority of therapist-guided interventions was not supported. The section then relates the findings back to prior exposure and VRET literature and makes a reasonable attempt to interpret the absence of group differences. The use of inhibitory learning and expectancy violation provides a coherent theoretical frame, and the student also offers plausible alternative explanations, such as the high structure of the self-guided intervention and limits of the outcome measure. The limitations are relevant and more specific than generic comments, especially the absence of follow-up and process measures. Future research suggestions also follow logically from these limitations. The main weaknesses are some repetition in the opening paragraph, a tendency to overstate what the findings 'suggest' given the limited design, and somewhat limited engagement with the fact that no differences were found despite a theory-driven prediction. The theoretical implications are present, but they could have been sharpened further by distinguishing more carefully between what was directly tested and what remains speculative. Still, this is a solid, coherent discussion for a second-year student paper.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric rightly emphasizes main conclusion, critical reflection, coherence, and responsible use of references. It could be strengthened by explicitly separating interpretation of findings, integration with theory/literature, limitations, and implications. Right now, a discussion with decent limitations but weak theoretical integration might receive a similar score to one with stronger interpretive depth. More fine-grained descriptors would improve consistency.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clearly written and easy to follow. The scientific tone is appropriate, paragraphs are usually well structured, and the reader can follow the overarching argument from introduction to discussion. Referencing is mostly responsible and the language is mostly correct. There are, however, several noticeable style and APA issues that keep the score from being higher. The paper contains repetition, most clearly in the first paragraph of the discussion where a sentence is duplicated. There are also some grammatical and phrasing issues, occasional inconsistency in tense, and some citation/reference inconsistencies in APA formatting. The placement of the results table at the end instead of within the Results section also weakens presentation. Overall, the writing is above sufficient and mostly clear, but not yet polished.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is generally clear and practical, especially for a student paper context. A useful refinement would be to distinguish more explicitly between errors that affect readability and minor APA/grammar imperfections that are normal at this level. As written, the rubric risks encouraging graders to overweigh surface issues unless they consciously use the calibration summary. Stronger anchoring to clarity, paragraph structure, and scientific tone over minor technical formatting would improve reliability.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and generally convincing line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, gap, research question, and hypotheses. The societal relevance is explained well and linked to treatment accessibility. The theoretical framework is stronger than average for this level: avoidance, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, presence, and autonomy are all connected to the proposed comparison. The required core studies are included and used to motivate the study. The research gap is also explicit: prior work focused mainly on therapist-guided VRET, leaving the role of guidance within VRET underexplored. The main limitation is that the literature synthesis is still somewhat sequential and occasionally more assertive than the cited evidence clearly supports. Some claims about autonomy and self-guided exposure are theoretically plausible but not always tightly grounded in direct evidence. In addition, the final design rationale could have been tied even more explicitly to the specific hypotheses. Still, the Introduction is coherent, relevant, and above average for a second-year paper.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures coherence, relevance, and responsible reference use well, but it could distinguish more clearly between summary of literature and actual synthesis of literature, since that is a central learning goal in this assignment. It may also help to explicitly mention theoretical integration, because a paper can have a clear RQ yet still use theory only superficially. Adding descriptors about how convincingly the gap is derived from prior work would make the levels easier to apply consistently.
methods_feedback: The Methods section describes a coherent design that matches the research question and hypotheses. Participants, inclusion and exclusion criteria, recruitment, random allocation, intervention duration, and the main outcome measure are all present. The intervention conditions are distinguishable and the mixed design is stated clearly. However, the section remains somewhat underdeveloped in important replicability details. The participant subsection misses required descriptive sample characteristics such as mean age, standard deviation, gender distribution, and compensation. The materials section only describes the LSAS-SR and does not provide full questionnaire details expected from the guide, such as an example item or more precise scoring interpretation. The intervention descriptions are understandable, but still somewhat global: it remains unclear exactly how therapist guidance differed operationally from app guidance, how in vivo tasks were standardized to the VR tasks, and how adherence was monitored. The procedure also includes ethics references that typically do not belong there according to the guide, while key procedural details such as session order, timing of posttest, and debriefing are brief. Overall, the method is adequate and coherent, but not fully complete.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is useful in emphasizing coherence with the RQ and completeness of participants, materials, and procedure. However, the distinction between 'somewhat comprehensibly,' 'complete,' and 'clearly related' remains fairly broad. It would help if the rubric specified core required elements such as allocation, inclusion/exclusion criteria, sample characteristics, operationalization of all conditions, and sufficient procedural detail for replication at student level. That would improve consistency between graders.
results_feedback: The Results section is understandable and broadly aligned with the stated design: it reports the mixed ANOVA, assumption checks, main effects, interaction, and post-hoc comparisons. The interpretation of the pattern is also straightforward and consistent with the hypotheses. However, compared with the sample template and course expectations, the section is incomplete. A demographics table is missing, and the results table is not properly integrated into the section layout. The placement of the raw table text after the reference list suggests formatting problems. The reporting includes means and standard deviations for the main outcome, which is good, but there is no clear full table presentation within the section itself. The ANOVA reporting is mostly acceptable, though the effect size for the interaction is implausibly reported as partial eta squared smaller than .001 despite a nonzero F, which suggests some inaccuracy. There is also no reporting of sample use, missing data, or outlier handling. For this course level, the section is mostly correct but not complete enough to reach a higher score.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric correctly focuses on whether analyses and reporting are correct, complete, coherent, and relevant. Still, it is somewhat underspecified for this course context. Since the calibration and sample results stress demographics tables, descriptive statistics tables, assumption checks, and post-hoc reporting, these expectations could be reflected more explicitly in the rubric. As written, two papers with quite different levels of completeness might both seem to fit 'mostly correct' or 'complete.'
discussion_feedback: The Discussion provides a clear answer to the research question and states that the hypothesis was only partly supported: all interventions reduced social anxiety, but guided interventions did not outperform self-guided VRET. The section interprets the main findings rather than merely repeating them, and it connects them back to the inhibitory learning framework and earlier VRET literature. The student also addresses the unexpected null difference between conditions and proposes several plausible explanations, such as strong standardization, the broad outcome measure, and the possibility that core exposure principles were adequately implemented across groups. This is a strength. Limitations and future directions are relevant and mostly study-specific, especially the lack of follow-up and process measures. The broader implication that self-guided VRET may be a promising accessible alternative also follows reasonably from the findings. The main weaknesses are that the theory integration remains somewhat one-sided and confirmatory, with limited exploration of what the null interaction means for the autonomy argument specifically. Some interpretations go slightly beyond the data because no process measures were actually collected. There is also a small repetition error in the opening paragraph. Overall, the Discussion is coherent and above average, though not fully developed at the highest level.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes the line of reasoning to the main conclusion and the relevance of critical reflection. It could be strengthened by explicitly separating several dimensions that matter in this course: interpretation of expected versus unexpected findings, integration with theory and prior research, limitations tied to the actual design, and implications that follow from the data. At present, these are implied but not clearly differentiated, which may make grading less transparent.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clearly written and easy to follow. Paragraphs are mostly well structured, and the scientific tone is appropriate for the assignment. The argument is signposted clearly, especially in the Introduction and Discussion. Referencing is mostly responsible and sufficiently consistent for this level. There are some language and formatting issues that prevent a higher score: repeated sentences in the Discussion opening, a few awkward or overly long sentences, some APA inconsistencies in capitalization and punctuation in the reference list, and visible formatting problems around the results table placement. There is also some redundancy, especially where points are restated more than necessary. Still, overall readability is good and the language does not impede understanding.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is relatively clear and practical, especially in linking structure, grammar, APA, clarity, and redundancy. One improvement would be to distinguish more explicitly between issues that affect readability and issues that are mostly cosmetic. For early-stage student papers, that distinction is important to avoid over-penalizing minor APA or language errors. It may also help to include coherence and signposting at section level more explicitly, since these are central to scientific argumentation.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and generally coherent argumentative line toward the research question. Societal relevance is established early and linked reasonably well to the treatment gap and the potential value of scalable interventions. The theoretical framework is stronger than average for this level: avoidance, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, safety behavior, and presence are all explained in a way that supports the hypotheses. The three required core studies are included, as is an additional article fitting the specific focus on self-guided VRET. Importantly, prior studies are not only summarized but are mostly used as building blocks leading to the gap about guidance within VRET. The research question and hypotheses are explicit and aligned with the preceding reasoning. Weaknesses remain: the societal relevance section is somewhat long and could be more concise; some claims are slightly overstated relative to the evidence; and the comparison between self-guided VRET and in vivo exposure is less theoretically elaborated than the comparison within VRET. Still, the section is solidly above average in reasoning and synthesis for this course level.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing argumentation, synthesis, and the link from literature to RQ/hypotheses. A possible improvement would be to operationalize more clearly how assessors should weigh missing required content from the writing guide versus weaknesses in coherence. It may also help to distinguish more explicitly between 'study-by-study summary' and genuine synthesis with concrete indicators, since this is a central grading difficulty.
methods_feedback: The Methods describe a coherent design that matches the research question and hypotheses. Participants, inclusion/exclusion criteria, recruitment, random assignment, overall design, and the main dependent measure are all present. The interventions are described in a structured way and the student makes a clear effort to standardize conditions across groups, which supports internal validity. This fits the rubric's adequate range well. The main reason the grade is not higher is that several important details are still missing for replication at the expected student level: no participant demographics beyond age range and intended sample size are given, despite the guide requiring mean age, SD, and gender; no compensation or reward is reported; no concrete diagnostic procedure for establishing SAD is described; the materials section is incomplete because the LSAS-SR description lacks developer/reference support specific to the self-report version and gives limited detail compared with the guide; and procedural information is partly mixed into Materials/Interventions. The method is understandable and mostly complete, but not fully complete according to the writing guide.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric captures coherence and completeness well, but it could be more explicit about which missing elements are considered major versus minor at this student level. For example, demographics, allocation details, compensation, diagnostic procedure, and subsection placement could be listed as anchor points. That would improve consistency between graders without making the rubric too rigid.
results_feedback: The Results section is understandable and the chosen analysis matches the stated mixed design. Assumption checks are reported, the main effects and interaction are given with F values, degrees of freedom, p values, and effect sizes, and post-hoc comparisons are included. This shows a reasonable grasp of the expected structure. However, the section falls around adequate rather than good because several required sample-based elements from the guide and calibration summary are missing or underdeveloped. There is no demographics table. Table 1 is announced but not properly integrated in the section and the formatting/content are incomplete relative to the sample template. The figure is mentioned but not actually presented in the paper text as submitted. Results reporting is also slightly inconsistent: if post-hoc tests found all groups improved, the section would benefit from clearer reporting of the actual mean patterns directly in the text. In addition, there is no explicit note on handling outliers or missing data. The analysis is mostly correct and coherent, but the section does not fully meet the sample-based expectations.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric benefits from the connection to the sample section, which gives concrete expectations. Still, the rubric could better separate statistical correctness from completeness of reporting. It would help to specify whether missing one table, missing a figure, or missing demographic descriptives should each lower the score by a similar amount, because these omissions currently require substantial grader discretion.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is one of the stronger parts of the paper. It clearly restates the aim, answers the research question, and indicates that the hypothesis about overall improvement was supported whereas the hypothesis about superiority of guided interventions was not. The student interprets the findings rather than merely repeating them and links the interpretation back to the inhibitory learning framework, expectancy violation, and prior literature. The comparison with earlier studies is meaningful and the paper explains the unexpected null differences between conditions with several plausible alternative interpretations, including standardization of the self-guided condition and the possibility that the chosen outcome measure was too global. Limitations are study-specific and well connected to future research directions. Broader implications are also discussed in a way that reasonably returns to the societal relevance. The main limitation preventing an even higher grade is that some interpretations are still somewhat speculative because no process measures were included, and the discussion could engage a bit more critically with the absence of between-group effects rather than leaning quickly toward practical optimism. Still, this is a strong, above-average discussion for a second-year student.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes interpretation, linkage to theory, and study-specific limitations. A useful refinement would be to add clearer anchors for how to evaluate discussions of null findings or unexpected findings, since these are common in student papers and often separate average from stronger work. Explicit mention of overclaiming practical implications could also sharpen grading consistency.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally clear, readable, and organized in a scientific style appropriate for the course level. Terminology is mostly consistent, sectioning is clear, and the argument is easy to follow. There are, however, enough language and APA-style issues to keep this in the adequate-to-good border area rather than clearly good. The most visible language issue is repetition, including a duplicated sentence in the first discussion paragraph. There are also some wording/grammar inconsistencies, capitalization inconsistencies, and several APA/reference issues in the bibliography and citations. A few references appear inaccurately formatted, and the Results/table integration is untidy. These issues do not seriously impede understanding, but they are too frequent to call the writing nearly faultless.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is broad and practical, especially in protecting content grades from being overly penalized for writing issues. However, some criteria rely on counting errors, which may be hard to apply consistently and may not reflect severity well. It may be useful to complement the count-based approach with clearer descriptors of how much the writing affects readability, professionalism, and structural clarity.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and mostly coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, prior research, and the research question. Societal relevance is strong and clearly connected to treatment accessibility and the potential value of VRET. The theoretical framework is more developed than average for this level: avoidance, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, and autonomy are all linked to the proposed comparison. The required core studies are included and used functionally rather than only descriptively, and the additional self-guided VRET study fits the research aim well. The research question and hypotheses are explicit and logically follow from the preceding argument. The main limitation preventing a higher score is that parts of the introduction become somewhat lengthy and occasionally over-argued, with some claims resting on broader theoretical extrapolation rather than directly on the reviewed empirical literature. In addition, the transition from general VRET effectiveness to the specific prediction about guidance could be a bit tighter. Still, this is clearly in the good range.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is broadly well aligned with the course goals because it prioritizes reasoning, synthesis, and the line toward the research question. One improvement would be to operationalize more explicitly how much weight should be given to the required writing-guide components versus overall coherence, since a paper can be strong in argumentation but still miss one formal element. The phrase 'at least 60%/80% of the conclusions are convincing' is also difficult to apply consistently in practice and could be replaced with more concrete indicators of argumentative quality.
methods_feedback: The Methods section is coherent and aligned with the research question and hypotheses. Participants, core inclusion and exclusion criteria, the main measure, intervention conditions, and the overall design are all present. The interventions are described clearly enough to understand the intended differences between conditions, and the attempt to standardize duration and structure across groups is appropriate. However, the section lacks several details that the writing guide expects. Participant information is incomplete because no mean age, standard deviation, gender distribution, allocation details beyond randomization, or reward/compensation are reported. The Materials section is also limited: only the LSAS-SR is described, without developer/reference details for the self-report version, example item, or fuller scoring/cutoff information. Some intervention description is somewhat procedural and expansive, while procedure omits practical details such as session location logistics, timing of posttest, and debriefing. Overall, the study is replicable at a broad level, but one to two important details are missing, placing it in the adequate range.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately emphasizes coherence with the research question and completeness relative to the writing guide. It could be improved by distinguishing more clearly between missing descriptive details that are important but not fatal at this level (e.g., reward information) and missing design-critical details that harm replicability (e.g., allocation procedure, timing of assessments). More explicit anchors for what counts as 'one or two important details' versus 'multiple important details' would likely increase inter-rater consistency.
results_feedback: The Results section reports the main analysis in a generally understandable way and uses an analysis appropriate to the stated design. Assumptions are checked, the main effects and interaction are reported with test statistics, and post-hoc comparisons are described. The pattern of results is also interpreted at the operational level. However, compared with the sample and rubric expectations, the section is incomplete. The demographics table is missing, and the outcome table is referred to but not properly integrated in standard results-section format. There is also no full figure presented beyond a caption reference. The reporting is therefore weaker than the sample benchmark. In addition, there is a potential inconsistency between the very large observed mean decreases and the reported partial eta-squared for time, which raises some concern about reporting accuracy, though the overall analytical structure is still coherent. This fits the adequate range rather than good.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is useful in combination with the sample section, especially because the sample makes expectations concrete. A possible improvement would be to specify more directly which missing elements are most consequential: demographics table, descriptive means table, assumptions, post-hoc tests, and figure likely do not all carry equal weight. It may also help to clarify how to grade sections that use the correct statistical test and structure but omit one or two presentational elements from the sample.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is strong for this course level. It begins with a clear answer to the research question and states that the hypothesis was only partly supported. The findings are meaningfully interpreted rather than merely restated, and the student connects the results back to inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, autonomy, and the earlier literature. The absence of differences between interventions is not ignored; instead, several plausible explanations are discussed, including standardization, possible threshold effects of exposure, and limitations of the outcome measure. The section also includes study-specific limitations and sensible future directions, especially regarding follow-up, other populations, and process measures. Practical relevance is implied through accessibility and self-guided treatment potential. The main reasons it does not reach the excellent range are some repetition in the opening paragraph, limited explicit return to the broader societal implications in a fully developed final implication paragraph, and a few interpretations that are somewhat more confident than the data warrant given the limited design and absence of follow-up/process measures.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the most important features well: conclusion, interpretation, links to theory and prior research, and critical reflection. It would benefit from an even clearer distinction between merely restating findings with citations and genuinely interpreting findings in relation to theory. In addition, it may help to include broader implications as a separate explicit criterion or subcriterion, since the writing guide emphasizes returning to societal relevance but the rubric gives that less visible weight.
lang_style_feedback: Overall language use is clear, academic, and easy to follow. Terminology is largely consistent, and paragraphing is mostly well structured. The paper reads as scientifically appropriate for a second-year student and generally maintains a coherent formal tone. There are, however, several noticeable issues: some repetition, especially in the Discussion opening; occasional awkward phrasing; a few grammar and spelling issues; and multiple APA/reference inconsistencies in capitalization, formatting, spacing, and citation details. These do not impede understanding, so they should affect only the Language & Style component. This places the paper in the good-to-adequate boundary, with 7.5 justified because readability and structure are clearly above basic satisfactory level.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is comprehensive, but some criteria may be difficult to apply reliably because they depend on counting error types rather than judging their impact on readability. A clearer separation between APA accuracy, sentence-level language quality, and structural clarity could help. It may also be useful to add guidance on how to weigh frequent minor APA inconsistencies against otherwise very clear academic writing, especially given the instruction not to let style errors spill into content grades.

intro_feedback: De introductie laat een duidelijke en overwegend coherente redenering zien van maatschappelijke relevantie naar theoretisch kader, eerdere literatuur, kennislacune en uiteindelijk de onderzoeksvraag en hypotheses. De maatschappelijke relevantie is vroeg aanwezig en goed verbonden aan toegankelijkheid en schaalbaarheid van behandeling. Het theoretisch kader is duidelijker uitgewerkt dan gemiddeld voor dit niveau, met een bruikbare koppeling tussen vermijding, exposure, inhibitory learning en de mogelijke rol van autonomie/begeleiding. Ook de drie verplichte kernstudies zijn opgenomen, plus aanvullende literatuur die aansluit bij de specifieke focus op zelfgeleide VRET. Sterk is dat de literatuur niet alleen wordt opgesomd, maar functioneert als opbouw naar de vraag naar de rol van begeleiding binnen VRET. Wel zijn er enkele zwakkere schakels. De koppeling tussen zelfdeterminatietheorie/autonomie en daadwerkelijke behandeluitkomsten blijft deels speculatief en had kritischer onderbouwd kunnen worden. Daarnaast worden de kernstudies soms iets te globaal samengevat, waardoor hun precieze bijdrage aan de gekozen designvergelijking niet altijd maximaal scherp is. Ook is de maatschappelijke relevantie wat lang uitgesponnen in plaats van echt compact als openingsparagraaf. Desondanks voldoet de sectie duidelijk aan de criteria voor een goede tot bovengemiddelde introductie.
intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is inhoudelijk sterk, maar de grens tussen 'adequate' en 'good' hangt nu vrij sterk op globale formuleringen als 'meestal gesynthetiseerd' of '80% overtuigend'. Dat maakt interbeoordelaarsbetrouwbaarheid lastig. Het zou helpen om explicieter te operationaliseren wat telt als echte synthese versus samenvatting, en hoeveel van de verplichte bouwstenen minimaal inhoudelijk uitgewerkt moeten zijn. Ook zou de rubric kunnen verduidelijken hoe zwaar de kwaliteit van het theoretisch kader weegt ten opzichte van de bespreking van de vier kernartikelen.
methods_feedback: De methode is coherent en sluit in grote lijnen aan op de onderzoeksvraag en hypotheses. De belangrijkste onderdelen zijn aanwezig: deelnemers, inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, interventies, procedure en design. De beschrijving van de drie condities maakt het algemene idee van de manipulatie goed begrijpelijk, en de keuze om sessieduur en opbouw te standaardiseren helpt de interne logica van het ontwerp. Toch ontbreken meerdere details die volgens de schrijfwijzer belangrijk zijn. Bij participanten ontbreken bijvoorbeeld gemiddelde leeftijd, standaarddeviatie, geslachtsverdeling, beloning/compensatie en concrete informatie over toewijzing aan groepen behalve randomisatie in algemene zin. In de materialen is alleen de LSAS-SR beschreven; essentiële details zoals een bron voor de self-reportversie of psychometrische informatie zijn beperkt, en de interventies staan in een aparte sectie maar zijn nog niet volledig replicabel beschreven. Bij de procedure worden ethische goedkeuring en globale volgorde genoemd, maar duur, locatie/setting per conditie en exacte uitvoering van de sessies blijven vrij algemeen. Ook ontbreekt een analysegedeelte als aparte methodecomponent, terwijl dat volgens de richtlijnen wel verwacht mag worden. Dit is dus een adequate methode, maar niet volledig uitgewerkt.
methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek sluit redelijk goed aan op de schrijfwijzer, maar kan concreter worden gemaakt door de vereiste elementen expliciet te noemen in de prestatieniveaus, zoals demografische kerngegevens, allocatie, compensatie, instrumentdetails en analysemethode. Nu blijft 'meerdere belangrijke details' wat vaag. Ook zou nuttig zijn om beter te onderscheiden tussen een methode die inhoudelijk coherent is maar onvolledig, en een methode die fundamenteel niet repliceerbaar is.
results_feedback: De resultaten zijn begrijpelijk en de gekozen analyse past bij het beschreven design. Er wordt een mixed ANOVA gerapporteerd, aannames worden besproken, hoofd- en interactie-effecten worden vermeld en er worden post-hocvergelijkingen beschreven. Dat zijn duidelijke pluspunten. Tegelijkertijd blijft de sectie onder het niveau van het meegeleverde voorbeeld en de rubricverwachtingen. Er ontbreekt een demografische tabel volledig, terwijl die volgens de calibratie expliciet verwacht wordt. Daarnaast wordt naar Tabel 1 en Figuur 1 verwezen, maar de resultatenpresentatie is onvolledig geïntegreerd: de tabelopmaak is niet echt uitgewerkt in de sectie zelf en er is geen volledige figuurbeschrijving zoals in het voorbeeld. Ook worden geen exacte post-hoccontraststatistieken gegeven, alleen de conclusies en p-waarden. Verder is er een kleine inhoudelijke onzorgvuldigheid in de interpretatie van partial eta squared voor de interactie en in de rapportageconsistentie rond de LSAS/LSAS-SR-benaming. Voor dit niveau is de kern aanwezig en grotendeels correct, maar er missen één à twee belangrijke elementen die het resultaatgedeelte meer voorbeeldconform hadden gemaakt.
results_rubric_feedback: De resultatenrubriek profiteert van de koppeling aan het sample results document, maar de criteria mogen explicieter specificeren welke elementen verplicht zijn: demografische tabel, descriptieve tabel voor uitkomstmaten, assumptiechecks, hoofdeffecten/interactie, post-hoc tests en figuur. Nu staat dit deels buiten de rubric in toelichtende tekst. Het zou ook helpen om aan te geven in hoeverre exacte APA-statistische rapportage meeweegt versus inhoudelijke volledigheid en begrijpelijkheid.
discussion_feedback: De discussie is sterk en duidelijk bovengemiddeld voor dit niveau. De eerste alinea geeft een helder antwoord op de onderzoeksvraag en relateert de bevindingen direct aan de hypotheses. Vervolgens worden de resultaten inhoudelijk geïnterpreteerd in plaats van alleen herhaald. De koppeling aan eerdere literatuur en aan het theoretisch kader is goed zichtbaar, vooral via inhibitory learning, expectancy violation en de mogelijke rol van autonomie. Ook het onverwachte resultaat — geen verschil tussen begeleide en zelfgeleide VRET — wordt serieus genomen en voorzien van plausibele alternatieve verklaringen. De beperkingen zijn redelijk studiespecifiek, zoals het ontbreken van follow-up, het niet meten van procesmaten en de beperkte generaliseerbaarheid. De aanbevelingen voor toekomstig onderzoek volgen logisch uit die beperkingen. Een klein zwakker punt is dat de bredere maatschappelijke/praktische implicaties wel aanwezig zijn, maar relatief beknopt blijven in verhouding tot de sterke maatschappelijke opening in de introductie. Daarnaast had nog iets kritischer kunnen worden besproken dat de conclusie over gelijkwaardige effectiviteit beperkt blijft tot de specifieke, gestandaardiseerde onderzoekscontext. Toch is de sectie in argumentatieve kwaliteit en samenhang duidelijk goed.
discussion_rubric_feedback: De discussierubriek dekt de belangrijkste vaardigheden goed, vooral interpretatie, koppeling aan theorie en kritische reflectie. Wel blijven termen als 'enigszins betekenisvol' en 'goed gelinkt' relatief breed. Meer concrete ankers zouden nuttig zijn, bijvoorbeeld afzonderlijk benoemen van: expliciete beantwoording van de RQ, bespreking van hypothesesteun, interpretatie van onverwachte bevindingen, studie-specifieke beperkingen en praktische implicaties. Dat zou de rubric transparanter en consistenter toepasbaar maken.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen helder, goed leesbaar en passend wetenschappelijk van toon. Terminologie is meestal consistent en de opbouw van alinea’s is logisch. De introductie en discussie hebben duidelijke signposting en een goed te volgen argumentatieve structuur. Er zijn wel meerdere stijl- en vormproblemen die een hoger cijfer verhinderen. Zo komt er herhaling voor, bijvoorbeeld een dubbel geformuleerde zin in de eerste alinea van de discussie. Ook zijn er enkele grammaticale en formuleringstechnische onzorgvuldigheden, zoals congruentieproblemen, kleine interpunctiefouten en soms wat omslachtige zinnen. In APA en referentiestijl zitten meerdere onvolkomenheden, waaronder inconsistent hoofdlettergebruik, enkele verdachte of minder passend gebruikte bronnen, kleine formatfouten en inconsistentie in benamingen. Deze fouten belemmeren het begrip niet echt, maar ze zijn wel duidelijk aanwezig. Daarom past een adequate maar niet bijna-foutloze beoordeling.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: De taal- en stijlrubriek is bruikbaar, maar sterk foutentellend geformuleerd. Dat maakt beoordeling soms mechanisch, terwijl leesbaarheid en wetenschappelijke helderheid ook afhangen van ernst en spreiding van fouten. Het zou beter zijn om explicieter te wegen hoe sterk fouten het begrip en de professionele indruk daadwerkelijk beïnvloeden. Ook kan de rubric onderscheid maken tussen APA-fouten in de lopende tekst, referentielijst en statistische rapportage, omdat die niet altijd even zwaar wegen.

intro_feedback: The Introduction is above average for this course level. It opens clearly with societal relevance, defines SAD, explains why young adults are an important target group, and motivates the clinical relevance of VRET well. The paper also includes both theoretical background and prior research, and the final research aim and hypotheses are explicit and logically related to the question. A strength is that the student goes beyond simple summary by building toward the comparison between therapist-guided and self-guided VRET. The inclusion of the required core VRET studies is helpful and generally responsible. The main reason this is not higher is that the line of reasoning is not always equally tight.
