However, several details that matter for methodological completeness are underdeveloped or slightly inconsistent. The LSAS-SR is described inaccurately as a screening tool for generalized anxiety disorder rather than social anxiety disorder. The Materials section for the intervention focuses on brand names and prices, which is not very useful scientifically, while key treatment-standardization details are less precise. Allocation is mentioned, but the randomization procedure is basic and not fully justified. Procedure and Treatment overlap somewhat, and some material that could have been integrated under Materials is instead spread across sections. There is also no explicit analytic subsection. These issues keep it from the good range, but the study design remains understandable and mostly aligned with the paper's aims.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is clear about coherence and completeness, but it could benefit from a more explicit checklist of essential design elements for this assignment level, especially allocation, timing, participant characteristics, and intervention standardization. That would improve inter-rater consistency. The criterion about information being in the wrong place is useful, though it may need clarification on when this truly hinders understanding versus when it is just a stylistic issue.
results_feedback: The Results section is mostly correct, coherent, and relevant to the stated design, which fits the adequate range. It includes the expected core elements for this course level: a description of the sample used, mention of outlier screening, a demographics table, reporting of the mixed ANOVA, assumption checks, main effects, interaction effect, post-hoc comparisons, and a figure. The overall reporting follows the sample structure reasonably well and the conclusions drawn from the reported statistics are consistent with the descriptive pattern. However, the section is not fully complete or polished enough for the good range. The tables are referred to but not integrated cleanly into the section as written, and Table 2 is necessary for evaluating the reporting quality. Assumption checks are somewhat selective and brief. Some reporting is less precise than ideal, for example calling LSAS-SR scores “average scores” while reporting raw means, and there is limited detail on effect sizes or fuller interpretation of assumptions. There is also a reference in the Results section, which the writing guide/sample discourages. Overall, it is a solid student-level Results section, but not as complete and cleanly executed as the sample baseline for 7.5.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is helpful because it anchors expectations in the provided sample, which is concrete and student-friendly. It might be improved by distinguishing more clearly between missing statistical elements and weaker presentation quality. For example, students who include all required analyses but report them somewhat awkwardly may differ meaningfully from students who omit core tables or post-hoc tests. A clearer indication of whether effect sizes are optional or desirable would also help.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is in the good range because it provides a clear main conclusion, meaningfully interprets the findings, and links them back to both prior literature and theory. The opening paragraph directly answers the research question and states that the hypothesis was only partly supported, which is appropriate. The student does more than restate results: they interpret why therapist-led treatment may have outperformed self-led treatment and engage with the unexpected maintenance of self-led effects over time. That comparison with Lindner et al. and the attempt to explain the discrepancy through broader fear generalization is a real strength. The discussion also includes study-specific limitations, particularly the absence of a waiting-list control and the inability to monitor engagement in the self-led condition, and these are tied to concrete future research suggestions. The broader implications return to treatment access and societal relevance. The main reason the section does not reach excellent is that some interpretations go beyond what the data can firmly support, especially the suggestion that self-led gains may reflect spontaneous recovery or regression to the mean without direct evidence. The theoretical implications are present but could be developed more explicitly in terms of which aspects of the framework were tested and which remain untested.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes interpretation, linkage to introduction/theory, and study-specific limitations. A useful refinement would be to separate 'comparison to prior research' and 'theoretical implications' more explicitly, because a student can do one better than the other. It may also help to define more concretely what counts as a study-specific limitation versus a generic one, as this is a common judgment call in grading.
lang_style_feedback: The Language and Style are in the good-to-adequate range, best captured by a 7.5. The paper is generally clear, readable, and appropriately scientific in tone. Paragraphing is logical, terminology is mostly consistent, and the reader can follow the argument without difficulty. The Introduction and Discussion in particular are well signposted. There are, however, several APA and reference-format issues, some inconsistencies in citation years, and a few awkward or imprecise formulations. The reference list contains noticeable formatting irregularities and some bibliographic inaccuracies. There are also occasional wording choices that reduce precision, such as minor terminology slips and some redundancy. These are not serious enough to impede understanding, so they should not lower the scientific reasoning grades, but they do keep the Language & Style score below the upper good range.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is comprehensive and appropriately prevents language issues from overly affecting scientific reasoning scores. One improvement would be to clarify how many APA/reference errors count as 'different errors,' since assessors may count repeated formatting problems differently. The rubric could also distinguish more explicitly between stylistic elegance and functional clarity, so that clear but not polished papers are easier to place consistently.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear and mostly coherent line of reasoning from societal relevance to theory, previous research, and the final research question. The paper explains SAD and why improved treatment matters, then builds toward VR exposure and the possible added value of group delivery. A clear hypothesis is stated, and the study is relevant given prior work. The theoretical discussion around avoidance, expectancy violation, inhibitory learning, and possible group processes is reasonably well connected to the hypothesis. The literature is generally used responsibly and the argument does more than merely list studies. That said, the structure is not always tight. Some paragraphs are repetitive, and parts of the previous-research section contain inaccuracies or overinterpretations of what earlier studies establish. The required studies are included, but their integration is sometimes uneven, and the distinction between CBT plus VR, VR-only exposure, and group versus individual format is not always handled with full precision. There are also some questionable or less appropriate references for key claims and some imprecise phrasing. Overall, though, the introduction is coherent, relevant, and above average for this level.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the key construct well by focusing on line of reasoning, relevance, clarity of the RQ, and responsible use of references. A useful improvement would be to distinguish more explicitly between literature summary and literature synthesis, because that is one of the central course goals and currently sits somewhat implicitly inside 'coherent and convincingly argued.' It may also help to mention alignment between theory, prior research, and hypotheses more directly in the descriptor.
methods_feedback: The Methods section describes a coherent study that matches the research question: a randomized comparison of group VR, individual VR, and waitlist with pre-post assessment. The main subsections are present and the overall design is understandable. Participants, conditions, the main measure, and the broad procedure are described clearly enough for a reader to follow the study. However, several required details are missing or inconsistent. The participant description is incomplete and somewhat confusing: the mean age appears malformed, allocation is stated but group-specific demographics are not summarized in the section itself, and the inclusion/exclusion criteria are poorly phrased and internally inconsistent, especially around diagnosis timing and pharmacological treatment. The materials description gives some useful information about the VR setup and LSAS-SR, but the questionnaire description is not fully complete in the expected format and the reliability statement is too vague. There is also some mixing of intervention content and procedure. The Procedure is understandable, but still somewhat sparse in terms of exact timing and standardization. So the method is coherent and mostly complete, but not yet fully precise or cleanly specified.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is broadly useful, but the categories 'complete and correct' versus 'described comprehensibly' remain somewhat general. Because this course has concrete expectations in the writing guide, the rubric could be improved by naming key required elements more explicitly, such as allocation, inclusion/exclusion criteria, participant characteristics, operationalization of variables, and enough procedural detail for basic replication. That would make grading more transparent and consistent.
results_feedback: The Results section is mostly correct, coherent, and clearly tied to the stated design. The student follows the expected structure reasonably well by reporting sample size, outliers, assumptions, the mixed ANOVA, and post-hoc comparisons. The main pattern of findings is communicated clearly and at the right operational level, and the interpretation of the significant interaction is appropriate. The inclusion of descriptive statistics and post-hoc tests matches the expectations for this assignment. This is around the level of the sample structure and therefore above adequate. The main weaknesses are in presentation quality and consistency. The tables are difficult to read and contain substantial formatting problems, repeated labels, and some confusing entries. There is also a mismatch in numbering and references to tables, and the text says normality was not violated while one post-treatment Shapiro-Wilk value in the table appears significant. In addition, the demographic presentation is cluttered and not cleanly separated from the main outcome reporting. These issues reduce polish and precision, but the statistical reasoning and core reporting remain mostly sound.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric appropriately emphasizes correctness, completeness, coherence, and relevance to the design. A helpful refinement would be to anchor 'complete' more concretely to expected student-level elements from the sample, such as demographics table, descriptive statistics per condition/time, assumption checks, omnibus test, and post-hoc comparisons when needed. This would better support consistent grading while still allowing flexibility in statistical detail.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion provides a clear main conclusion, answers the research question, and distinguishes between the supported and unsupported parts of the hypothesis. The student does more than restate the results; they attempt to explain why both VR conditions improved and why group VR may not have outperformed individual VR. The discussion meaningfully reconnects findings to theory, especially inhibitory learning and expectancy violation, and compares the findings with previous studies such as Kampmann et al. and Anderson et al. Limitations are study-specific rather than purely generic, and future research directions generally follow from those limitations. The final paragraph also returns to practical relevance, which strengthens the overall section. The main limitations are that some interpretations are somewhat speculative and not always tightly grounded in what the study can actually show. The theoretical implications could be developed more explicitly, for example by stating more clearly whether the framework is supported, challenged, or needs revision. Some claims in the limitations and implications sections are also asserted somewhat strongly relative to the data. Still, the reasoning is mostly coherent, relevant, and above average for this course level.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the essentials of conclusion and critical reflection, but it could better separate distinct components that are important in this course: interpretation of findings, connection back to theory and literature, limitations, and broader implications. At present these are partly bundled under 'reasoning culminating in the main conclusion' and 'critical reflection,' which can make distinctions between adequate and good performance harder to apply consistently.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language. The overall structure is recognizable, with clear sectioning and a visible attempt at formal academic style. Most paragraphs have a discernible focus, and the reader can usually follow the argument. However, the writing contains frequent awkward sentences, grammatical errors, punctuation problems, inconsistent wording, and some unclear or overly long constructions. There are also multiple APA and formatting issues in citations and references, as well as capitalization inconsistencies and occasional imprecise terminology. The tables especially contain major formatting problems that reduce readability. Redundancy appears in several sections, particularly in the Introduction and appended tables. Overall, the language and style are sufficient and mostly functional, but clearly not polished.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and practical, especially in identifying paragraph structure, grammar, APA, vagueness, and redundancy. One possible improvement would be to clarify how heavily formatting issues in tables/figures should weigh relative to prose quality, since in student papers these can strongly affect readability. It may also help to specify that minor APA errors should not dominate the score when scientific clarity remains strong.

intro_feedback: The Introduction presents a clear topic, establishes societal relevance, and arrives at a clear research question and hypothesis. The broad line of reasoning is coherent: SAD is important, exposure is effective but limited, VR may help, and group processes may add value beyond individual VR. The student also includes a theoretical account involving maladaptive cognitions, avoidance, inhibitory learning, and expectancy violation, and uses this to motivate the prediction that group VR may outperform individual VR. That said, the argumentation is only somewhat convincing rather than strongly persuasive. Some literature use is shaky or not optimally aligned with the assignment: the required studies are discussed, but Anderson et al. and Kampmann et al. are not always characterized with full precision, and an additional study is introduced in a way that partly distracts from the required core set. Several claims are under-supported or based on weak/non-ideal references for this context. There are also inaccuracies and imprecise formulations, and the storyline sometimes becomes repetitive. Overall, this is an adequate, around-average Introduction with a visible argumentative structure, but not yet a tightly synthesized and highly convincing one.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the core focus on line of reasoning, relevance, and hypothesis well, but it could be improved by making literature synthesis more explicit. At present, a paper can seem to meet the criterion with a largely study-by-study summary as long as the RQ is eventually clear. Adding explicit indicators about integrating theory with prior findings, and about motivating design choices from literature, would make the rubric more diagnostic for this assignment.
methods_feedback: The Methods section describes a coherent design that matches the research question: three conditions, random assignment, pre-post measurement, and LSAS-SR as the main outcome. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the overall study is understandable. However, several important details are vague, inconsistent, or incorrect enough to lower the grade somewhat. In Participants, the age reporting is incomplete/incorrectly formatted, and the inclusion and exclusion criteria are confusing (for example, phrases such as diagnosis 'no older than three years old' and medication 'not older than a year' are unclear and conceptually problematic). The sample description is also too limited relative to the writing guide. In Materials, the intervention descriptions are understandable but not precise enough for strong replicability, and the section mixes procedural information into Materials. The questionnaire description is partly adequate, but it lacks a full reference style treatment and more complete psychometric or administration detail. Procedure is chronologically organized and mostly clear, but timing and implementation details remain somewhat sparse. Overall, the Methods are nearly complete and mostly correct, but not fully complete and fully precise.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is clear at a broad level, but the distinction between 'developing' and 'adequate' could be operationalized more concretely. For this assignment, it would help if the rubric explicitly listed key required elements such as allocation, inclusion/exclusion criteria, compensation, demographic details, intervention comparability, instrument description, and chronological procedure. That would improve consistency between assessors and align more directly with the writing guide.
results_feedback: The Results section is generally the strongest part of the paper. It follows the expected sample-based structure reasonably well: sample size is stated, outliers are mentioned, descriptive statistics are referenced, assumptions are checked, the mixed ANOVA is reported, and post-hoc comparisons are described in plain language. The analysis is relevant to the stated design and procedure, and the conclusions drawn from the reported statistics are mostly correct. The section also includes multiple tables and interprets the interaction appropriately. Still, there are some limitations that prevent a higher grade. The presentation of tables is messy and clearly not well formatted, which affects readability. There is also some inconsistency in the normality reporting: the narrative says normality was not violated, but one reported post-treatment Shapiro-Wilk p-value in the table is .024. In addition, the demographics/statistics presentation is less clean than in the sample results model, and the labels/tables are somewhat confusing. Despite these issues, the statistical reasoning is mostly sound and complete for this course level.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric gives a useful general distinction between correctness, completeness, and coherence, but it is relatively broad compared with the detailed expectations in the sample results. It would be stronger if it explicitly mentioned core expected elements for this course level, such as demographics table, descriptive statistics by condition/time, assumption checks, main test, and post-hoc interpretation. This would help anchor grading more transparently.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion clearly restates the aim, answers the research question, and distinguishes supported from unsupported parts of the hypothesis. The student interprets the main pattern of findings, relates it back to inhibitory learning and expectancy violation, and discusses the null difference between group and individual VR rather than ignoring it. This is an important strength. The discussion also connects findings to prior studies and offers study-specific limitations, such as the implementation of the group condition and the wide age range, followed by future research suggestions. These are all positive signs of scientific reasoning at this level. However, the discussion remains only mostly coherent and nearly complete rather than fully compelling. Some interpretations are plausible but somewhat speculative, and the theoretical implications are not developed very deeply beyond returning to the same explanatory idea. The section also occasionally overstates what the findings imply for accessibility and treatment potential, given the modest design and lack of follow-up. Still, it is a solid, passable, around-average discussion that engages with the actual results in a meaningful way.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately emphasizes reasoning, conclusion, and critical reflection, but it could better separate distinct dimensions of quality. In particular, interpretation of expected versus unexpected findings, integration with theory, limitations, and implications are currently bundled together. A more fine-grained formulation would make it easier to distinguish a discussion that is coherent but superficial from one that is truly strong in theoretical integration and critical evaluation.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and uses mostly appropriate scientific language, but the writing quality is uneven. The overall structure of sections is clear, and most paragraphs have a recognizable main point. However, there are frequent grammar problems, awkward phrasing, punctuation issues, and APA/reference inconsistencies. Some sentences are unnecessarily long or imprecise, and wording occasionally becomes unclear in crucial places. There is also noticeable redundancy, especially in the Introduction, where similar points about exposure, VR, and group processes are repeated. Reference formatting contains multiple errors, and some source choices are not ideal for scientific writing. The Results tables are especially poorly formatted, which weakens presentation quality. Overall, the language and style are workable and do not prevent understanding, but they are below the level of a clearly polished paper.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is helpful in covering clarity, structure, grammar, APA, vagueness, and redundancy. One improvement would be to distinguish more clearly between errors that merely reduce polish and errors that meaningfully impede scientific argumentation. For student papers at this level, that distinction matters: assessors should be able to penalize messy APA and awkward wording without letting those issues overshadow otherwise adequate scientific reasoning.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear and generally coherent line of reasoning toward the research question. It begins with societal relevance, explains why SAD matters, introduces exposure and VR as treatment approaches, and builds toward the comparison between individual and group VR. The paper also makes a real attempt to use theory rather than only listing studies: maladaptive cognitions, safety behaviors, inhibitory learning, expectancy violation, and possible group mechanisms are linked to the hypothesis. The research question and main hypothesis are clear and relevant.

The main limitation is that the literature review is not always used as efficiently or accurately as it could be. Some study descriptions are somewhat imprecise or overstated, and the required articles are not always integrated in the strongest logical order. The argument sometimes becomes repetitive, especially around waitlist logic and group-process advantages. There are also several references that are weak, odd, outdated for the specific claim, or not ideal scientific support for central points. In addition, some conceptual distinctions are blurred, such as mixing VR exposure alone with CBT+VR frameworks without always clearly separating what each study adds.

Overall, though, this is an adequate-to-good Introduction for this course level: the RQ is motivated, theory is present, prior research is connected to the design, and the argument is mostly coherent, even if not fully tight or consistently precise.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the most important construct well: the quality of the line of reasoning toward the RQ and hypothesis. A useful refinement would be to make the role of theory versus literature synthesis more explicit, because students can appear coherent while still mainly summarizing studies one by one. It may also help to operationalize what counts as 'convincingly argued' at this course level, for example by specifying societal relevance, theoretical framework, integration of the required core articles, and a clear transition to design.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section is coherent and clearly linked to the stated research question and hypotheses. The basic design is understandable: three conditions, random assignment, pre-post measurement, LSAS-SR as outcome, and a 14-week intervention period. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, so the section is nearly complete and reasonably comprehensible.

The main weakness is that several important details are vague, inconsistent, or somewhat incorrect. The participant description is incomplete or confusing in places: the mean age appears to be missing a value, the wording around diagnosis age and medication timing is unclear ('no older than three years old', 'not older than a year'), and exclusion criteria are not always justified well. The Materials section does not fully describe the intervention protocol in enough detail to support replication at the expected level, and it mixes exposure with cognitive restructuring while the Introduction frames the study partly as VR exposure itself. The questionnaire description is acceptable but incomplete relative to the writing guide, because it lacks fuller citation details, clearer scoring explanation, and stronger psychometric support. Procedure is mostly chronological, but some details that matter for implementation are missing, such as how post-measurement timing was standardized, whether assessors were blinded, and how group sessions were organized across participants.

So this section is passable and coherent, but it remains somewhat under-specified and includes notable clarity problems that keep it below a solid average Methods score.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately emphasizes coherence with the RQ and completeness of participants, materials, and procedure. It could be strengthened by making required methodological elements more explicit, such as allocation, inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographics, measurement details, and enough procedural precision for approximate replication. Right now, 'complete and correct' leaves room for interpretation and may reduce consistency across graders.
results_feedback:
The Results section follows the expected overall structure reasonably well. It includes outlier inspection, assumption checks, a demographics/descriptive table, the mixed ANOVA, and Holm-corrected post-hoc comparisons. The reported interpretation of the main findings is consistent with the numbers shown: no baseline differences, significant reductions in both active conditions, no significant difference between group and individual VR, and both active conditions outperforming waitlist at post-test. That makes the section mostly correct, relevant, and understandable for this level.

At the same time, the reporting quality is uneven. The tables are poorly formatted and difficult to read, with repeated labels and clutter that substantially reduce clarity. There is some inconsistency between the narrative and the table numbering, and one normality result for post-waitlist appears significant in the table but is not discussed in the text. The demographics reporting is also awkwardly embedded in a very messy table rather than cleanly presented. In addition, although the analysis is largely appropriate, the Results do not consistently maintain a polished operational-level reporting style like the sample.

Overall, the section is adequate: the correct test was chosen, the main effects and interaction are interpreted appropriately, and the core findings are reported. However, technical and presentation issues prevent it from reaching a clearly good level.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric is broadly useful but somewhat compressed, especially because both the Good and Excellent columns are very similar except for statistical depth. For this course, it may help to include concrete anchors tied to the sample results, such as demographics table, descriptive statistics by condition/time, assumption checks, correct test choice, and post-hoc interpretation. That would improve inter-rater reliability and make it easier to distinguish adequate from good performance.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion is the strongest section of the paper. It starts with a clear restatement of the aim and hypotheses, answers the research question directly, and distinguishes supported from unsupported expectations. The student interprets the main pattern rather than only repeating the statistics, especially by discussing why both VR formats may have worked and why group VR may not have outperformed individual VR. The discussion also links findings back to the theoretical framework, particularly inhibitory learning and expectancy violation, and compares the results to prior studies such as Kampmann et al. and Anderson et al.

A further strength is that the paper does engage with the unexpected finding instead of ignoring it. The student offers a plausible interpretation about insufficiently activated group processes and derives future research suggestions from that limitation. The section also includes broader implications, returning to accessibility and clinical relevance.

The limitations are that some interpretations remain somewhat speculative and not always tightly grounded in the actual design. At times the argument stretches beyond what the data can support, for example when inferring why group mechanisms did not operate without direct measures of those processes. Some limitations are stronger than others; the age-range argument is plausible but somewhat secondary compared with more design-specific issues. The discussion of theory is solid but not deeply refined.

Overall, this is a good Discussion for a second-year paper: coherent, relevant, interpretive, and appropriately connected back to theory, prior work, limitations, and practical implications.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric correctly prioritizes the reasoning behind the main conclusion and the relevance of critical reflection. A possible improvement would be to separate interpretation of findings, integration with theory/literature, and critical evaluation into clearer subcriteria. At present, a paper can be strong in one of these areas and weaker in another, but the rubric gives limited guidance on how to weigh those differences.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally understandable and mostly uses scientific language appropriately. The overall structure is recognizable, and most sections and paragraphs have a clear function. The reader can follow the major argument from introduction to discussion.

However, there are quite a few language and style issues that lower the score. Sentences are often awkwardly phrased or grammatically incorrect, and punctuation is inconsistent. There are repeated wording problems, unclear formulations, and some imprecise academic phrasing. APA style also contains multiple errors in both references and in-text citation formatting, including inconsistent capitalization, punctuation, spacing, author formatting, and questionable source quality. The tables are especially poorly formatted and hurt readability. Some paragraphs are longer and more repetitive than necessary.

So while the language does not block understanding, the paper shows enough stylistic, grammatical, and APA problems that it fits better in the developing-to-adequate range than in the good range.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is useful in covering clarity, structure, grammar, APA, vagueness, and redundancy. It may benefit from clearer course-level anchors for what counts as acceptable APA and scientific style in a first research paper, because 'few' versus 'some' errors is still subjective. It could also distinguish readability problems in the running text from formatting problems in tables/figures, since both affect quality but not always equally.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning from societal relevance to treatment rationale, theory, prior research, and the final research question. The societal relevance is present early and the paper does define key ideas around SAD, exposure, and VR. The final aim and hypothesis are also stated clearly enough. A major strength is that the student tries to build an argument for why group VR might outperform individual VR, rather than only listing studies. The core studies are included and mostly used in a logical sequence.

The main limitation is that the synthesis is uneven. Several paragraphs read more like extended summaries or speculative reasoning than tightly argued building blocks toward the RQ. Some claims are insufficiently supported or not optimally linked to the cited source. There are also some inaccuracies or weak choices in source use for crucial claims, and the theoretical framework is only moderately integrated with the empirical literature. The argument does reach the RQ, but some links are weaker than they should be. Overall, this fits the adequate range: sound and mostly coherent, but not consistently strong or well-synthesized enough for a clearly higher grade.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is generally strong because it emphasizes argumentative coherence, synthesis, and connection to the RQ rather than mere presence of literature. A possible improvement would be to distinguish more explicitly between 'all required components are present' and 'the components are used functionally in the argument,' because these can diverge substantially in student work. It may also help to operationalize what counts as acceptable synthesis versus mostly summary with one or two concrete indicators.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section is coherent and the design matches the stated RQ: three conditions, pre-post assessment, and one primary outcome. Participants, materials, and procedure are all present, and the general study can be understood and roughly replicated. The random assignment, reward, treatment duration, and broad inclusion/exclusion logic are described.

However, there are multiple important detail problems that keep this from the good range. Participant reporting is incomplete or awkwardly phrased: the mean age appears to be missing its label/value formatting, group-specific demographics are not provided in the Methods, and the diagnostic criterion wording is confusing ('diagnosis ... no older than three years old'). Exclusion criteria about medication are also unclear. In Materials, the intervention descriptions are understandable, but some information is misplaced or insufficiently standardized. The LSAS-SR description is decent, but it lacks the developer citation in a clean form and gives only minimal psychometric information. Procedure is generally chronological, but some treatment details are repeated from Materials. Overall, the design is mostly complete and correct, but it lacks more than one important detail and contains some imprecision, so it falls in the adequate range.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is useful in focusing on coherence, completeness, and placement of information. It could be improved by specifying a clearer minimum checklist for this assignment level, especially for participants, allocation, intervention standardization, and measurement description. That would make grading more consistent when a section is broadly understandable but missing several medium-importance details.
results_feedback:
The Results section includes the expected main components for this course level: assumption checks, the mixed ANOVA, reporting of main effects and interaction, post-hoc tests, descriptive tables, and a figure reference. The reporting is broadly aligned with the sample structure, and the interpretation of the key interaction is understandable. The conclusion that both active conditions improved and did not differ from each other is supported by the reported analyses.

Still, the section has noticeable weaknesses. The tables are poorly formatted and difficult to read, which affects coherence. There is some inconsistency between the narrative and the tables, especially around normality and the listed p-values, and the numbering of tables is confusing. The student also refers to tables in a cluttered way, and one table includes age as a factor although that was not introduced in the Methods or reported in the main narrative as part of the planned analysis. Despite these issues, the core analysis and reporting are mostly correct and complete for this level. That places the section in the adequate range rather than clearly good.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric benefits from anchoring to the sample results, which is helpful for novice writers and graders. A potential improvement would be to clarify how heavily formatting problems versus analytic/reporting problems should weigh, since tables and figures may be messy while the actual statistical reasoning is acceptable. It may also help to say more explicitly how to grade results sections that include all required elements but contain one inconsistent or unexplained extra analysis.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion is the strongest section. It begins with a clear answer to the research question, distinguishes supported from unsupported parts of the hypothesis, and interprets the findings rather than only restating them. The student links the main positive findings back to exposure theory and to Kampmann et al. The unexpected null difference between group and individual VR is explicitly addressed and interpreted, which is an important strength.

The section also includes study-specific limitations and future directions that mostly follow from the actual findings, especially the point that the group condition may not have sufficiently activated interpersonal mechanisms. The paper returns to broader implications and societal relevance in a reasonable way.

The main weaknesses are that some explanations remain somewhat speculative, and links back to theory and prior studies are not always very precise or deeply developed. A few arguments are stronger rhetorically than empirically. Still, the overall reasoning is correct, coherent, and meaningfully connected to the introduction, with relevant study-specific reflection. This fits the good range.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric appropriately prioritizes interpretation, linkage to theory, comparison with prior literature, and study-specific limitations. A useful refinement would be to separate 'interpretation of expected results' from 'engagement with unexpected or null findings,' because student performance often differs strongly across those tasks. More explicit descriptors for what makes a limitation truly study-specific versus generic would also help calibration.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally understandable and the structure across major sections is clear. Headings are appropriate, the reader can follow the overall argument, and terminology is mostly consistent enough to preserve meaning.

However, language and style contain enough problems to lower this component. There are frequent grammatical and phrasing errors, awkward sentences, punctuation problems, capitalization inconsistencies, spacing issues, and APA/reference errors. Some sentences are vague or clumsy, and there is noticeable redundancy in places. Source formatting is inconsistent, several references appear incorrectly rendered, and table formatting is far from APA style. These issues usually do not make the content incomprehensible, but they do reduce clarity and polish. That places the paper in the developing range for Language & Style.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is comprehensive and appropriately separated from scientific reasoning. One challenge is that several criteria are quantified by error counts, which can be hard to apply consistently across papers of different lengths and may encourage impressionistic counting. It may help to supplement the counts with anchor examples of what constitutes minor, moderate, or clarity-impeding language problems at this course level.

intro_feedback:
The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning from societal relevance to treatment rationale, theory, prior research, and the final research question. The topic is introduced clearly and the paper does explain why VR exposure for SAD matters. A strength is that the student attempts to build an explicit theoretical framework around maladaptive cognitions, avoidance, and inhibitory learning, and uses that framework to motivate the comparison between individual and group VR formats. The research aim and hypothesis are also stated clearly at the end.

At the same time, the section is somewhat uneven in quality. The societal relevance is present, but it is more extended than necessary and sometimes drifts into general treatment description rather than sharply motivating this exact study. The synthesis of prior research is partly successful, but not consistently strong. The required core studies are all included, yet the discussion of them is not always accurate or optimally connected as building blocks. The paper sometimes overstates what previous studies imply, and the logic from Anderson et al. to the expectation that group VR should outperform individual VR is somewhat plausible but not fully convincing. There are also some questionable or weak source choices for crucial claims, and a few inaccuracies in conceptual framing and citation use reduce confidence in the argument. Overall, though, the argument is coherent and the RQ is justified well enough for an adequate-to-good level, with enough synthesis to place it at 7.0 rather than lower.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric is strong in emphasizing line of reasoning, synthesis, and connection from prior research to the RQ. A useful improvement would be to separate more explicitly between factual completeness requirements from the writing guide (e.g., all core studies present) and argumentative quality, because currently these can blend together. It may also help to clarify how much inaccuracy in the use of prior research should affect the grade when the overall argumentative flow remains coherent.
methods_feedback:
The Methods section is coherent and generally aligned with the stated research question and hypotheses. The basic structure with Participants, Materials, and Procedure is present, and the reader can broadly understand what the study design is: a three-condition randomized pre-post design comparing group VR, individual VR, and waitlist. The independent variable and main outcome measure are identified, and the procedure is described in chronological order.

However, several important details are missing, vague, or inconsistent. In Participants, the demographic information is incomplete or awkwardly reported: the mean age appears to be missing a label, group-specific demographics are absent from the prose, and inclusion/exclusion criteria are unclearly phrased ('diagnosis ... no older than three years old,' 'pharmacological therapy, not older than a year'). These criteria are difficult to interpret and weaken replicability. The Materials section also blends intervention description with procedural elements. The intervention is described reasonably, but standardization across conditions is not fully specified, and there is limited detail about who delivered treatment, whether therapists were the same across conditions, and how cognitive restructuring was incorporated despite the study being framed as exposure-focused. For the LSAS-SR, the student includes developer, item count, scale, score range, and example item, which is good, but reliability/validity support is minimal and the citation to the measure is not ideal. The Procedure is understandable but somewhat sparse regarding timing, consent, diagnostic confirmation details, and session structure. Overall, this is a coherent and mostly complete methods section, but it lacks multiple details that matter for precision and replication, placing it in the adequate range.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric appropriately focuses on coherence, completeness, and placement of information. It could be improved by making the distinction between 'one or two important details missing' and 'multiple important details missing' more concrete, perhaps with anchor examples such as allocation method, inclusion/exclusion criteria, demographics, timing, and operationalization details. That would likely improve grading consistency.
results_feedback:
The Results section generally follows the expected structure for this course: descriptive statistics are presented, assumptions are discussed, the main mixed ANOVA is reported, and post-hoc comparisons are included. The narrative description of the main findings is understandable and consistent with the reported hypothesis testing. The section also includes relevant tables and a figure reference, which aligns with the sample-based expectations.

Still, the section has several weaknesses that keep it from the good range. The presentation is somewhat messy and inconsistent: table numbering is confusing, Table 2 is referenced before being shown properly, and large portions of the output appear copied directly from statistical software without being cleaned into a reader-friendly format. A major issue is that the normality reporting in the prose is incomplete or partly inconsistent with the tables: one post-treatment Shapiro-Wilk value in the table is significant, but the written text states that normality was not violated. There is also some unnecessary inclusion of analyses involving age that are not explained in the method or integrated into the narrative. Despite these issues, the main statistical conclusions are coherent, the core tests are present, and the section is understandable enough for this level. Because all major expected elements are present but some are poorly presented or somewhat inconsistent, the Results merit a 7.0.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric benefits from the sample-based anchoring and is practical for this assignment. A possible refinement would be to distinguish more clearly between problems of statistical reasoning and problems of presentation/cleanup. For example, copied software output, messy tables, or numbering issues may not mean the analysis itself is poor. More explicit guidance on how to weigh minor inconsistencies versus major analytical errors would strengthen inter-rater reliability.
discussion_feedback:
The Discussion is the strongest section of the paper. It begins with a clear restatement of the aim and hypotheses, answers the research question directly, and distinguishes clearly between supported and unsupported hypotheses. The student meaningfully interprets the major pattern of findings rather than only repeating the results, and the discussion connects these interpretations back to inhibitory learning and expectancy violation theory. The paper also compares the findings to prior studies, especially Kampmann et al. and Anderson et al., in a way that is mostly relevant and understandable.

A notable strength is that the student seriously engages with the unexpected finding that group VR did not outperform individual VR. Rather than ignoring it, the paper offers plausible explanations related to the strength of the VR environment itself and the limited interpersonal processes in the group condition. The limitations are relatively study-specific rather than purely generic, especially the point about insufficiently facilitated group dynamics. Future research suggestions mostly follow from those limitations. The broader implications also return to the societal relevance in a reasonable way.

There are some weaknesses. The theoretical integration is good but not fully precise throughout, and some claims are a bit stronger than the design warrants. A few explanations remain speculative and are not always tightly tied to the actual data. The second limitation about age is plausible but less directly grounded in the reported results, because age was not meaningfully built into the study rationale or discussed analytically in the discussion. Even so, the discussion is coherent, relevant, and more interpretive than average, which places it in the good range.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric captures the most important dimensions well: conclusion, interpretation, linkage to introduction/theory, and critical reflection. It may help to add a clearer distinction between speculative but plausible interpretation and interpretation that overreaches beyond the data. That boundary is especially relevant in student papers, where thoughtful discussion should be rewarded without encouraging unsupported claims.
lang_style_feedback:
The paper is generally readable and the overall structure is clear, with recognizable sections and mostly understandable paragraphing. Terminology is usually consistent enough to follow the argument, and the student uses an appropriately scientific tone most of the time. The broad organization of the paper supports comprehension.

However, the Language & Style score is lowered by a fairly large number of writing and APA issues. There are repeated grammatical problems, awkward phrasing, punctuation errors, and unclear sentences. Some wording is imprecise or informal for scientific writing. APA style is also inconsistent in several places, including citation formatting, spacing, capitalization, source quality/use, and reference accuracy. There are clear signs of unedited statistical table output in the Results section, and some references are not ideally appropriate as foundational support for key claims. There is also some redundancy and occasional ambiguity in phrasing. These issues do not usually block understanding, but they are frequent enough to place the paper in the developing range for Language & Style.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and useful, especially in warning graders not to let writing issues overly affect other sections. One possible improvement would be to differentiate more clearly between APA formatting errors, inappropriate source selection, and broader stylistic clarity, since these can represent different skill areas. A compact checklist of the most common APA issues relevant to this assignment could also make judgments more consistent.

intro_feedback: The Introduction shows a clear overall line of reasoning from societal relevance to treatment rationale, theory, prior research, and finally the research question. The societal relevance is clearly established early, key concepts are defined, and the paper makes a reasonable attempt to explain why VR exposure may be useful for SAD. The theoretical framework around maladaptive cognitions, avoidance, and inhibitory learning is relevant and connected to the hypothesis. The research question and main hypothesis are also stated clearly at the end. A strength is that the student does more than simply list studies: there is some visible building-block logic from waitlist comparisons to active controls to the distinction between individual and group formats. That fits the rubric's adequate-to-good range. At the same time, the synthesis is uneven. Some studies are connected logically, but several transitions are a bit forced or overstated, and some conclusions go beyond what the cited evidence clearly supports. The use of the core studies is also imperfect: all required core articles are present, but Anderson et al. and Kampmann et al. are not always characterized with full precision relative to the proposed design, and the argument sometimes relies on less suitable or weaker sources for important claims. There are also credibility issues in the reference base for key claims, including some very recent or non-ideal sources and a few imprecise descriptions of treatments and mechanisms. Overall, the Introduction is sound, coherent, and clearly leads to the RQ, but the synthesis and evidential support are not consistently strong enough for a higher good/excellent score.
intro_rubric_feedback: The Introduction rubric captures the core priorities well, especially the importance of a coherent line of reasoning and the distinction between synthesis and mere summary. A useful refinement would be to make explicit how to weigh inaccuracies in the use of required core studies versus broader coherence of argumentation, because both matter but can pull grades in different directions. It may also help to specify how to judge source quality when students use non-ideal but not entirely irrelevant references for supporting claims. The current criteria are strong conceptually, but examples of what counts as 'one component written relatively poorly' versus 'multiple components written poorly' would improve grading consistency.
methods_feedback: The Methods section presents a coherent design that matches the stated research question: three conditions, pre-post measurement, and a clinically diagnosed SAD sample. The Participants, Materials, and Procedure subsections are all present, and the general structure is easy to follow. Random assignment, reward, and broad inclusion/exclusion criteria are included, which supports replicability at an acceptable second-year level. The Materials section also describes the intervention conditions and identifies the main outcome measure. However, the section lacks several important details expected in the writing guide. The participant description is incomplete and partly unclear: the mean age appears malformed, the allocation per condition is not explicitly reported in the Participants section, and some inclusion/exclusion criteria are phrased confusingly (for example, diagnosis 'no older than three years old' and medication exclusion 'not older than a year'). The Materials subsection gives only limited information on the LSAS-SR; it includes item count, scale, and score range, but not the original developers in proper form, no cutoff information, and only very minimal psychometric support. The intervention description is understandable but still somewhat vague in how group and individual conditions were standardized, and cognitive restructuring is included although the paper frames the comparison mainly as VR exposure, which creates some conceptual ambiguity. The Procedure is chronologically described and readable, but exact timing and some procedural specifics remain limited. Overall, this is coherent and mostly complete, but it misses one to several important details and contains some imprecision, placing it in the adequate range.
methods_rubric_feedback: The Methods rubric is clear in emphasizing coherence, completeness, and placement of information. A helpful improvement would be to operationalize what counts as 'one or two important details' missing versus 'multiple important details' missing, perhaps with examples tied to the writing guide such as allocation procedure, demographic information, instrument details, or timing. The criterion about information being in the wrong subsection is useful, but could distinguish between harmless misplacement and misplacement that creates conceptual confusion. Adding slightly more explicit guidance on how much replicability is expected at this student level would also support more consistent grading.
results_feedback: The Results section is generally aligned with the stated design and includes many of the expected components: outlier screening, assumption checks, a mixed ANOVA, main effects, the interaction, post-hoc comparisons, tables, and a figure reference. The reporting of the main statistical findings is understandable and largely coherent. The student also correctly interprets the interaction in broad terms and uses post-hoc tests to address the key group and time comparisons. This is solidly around the adequate range for this course level. Still, there are noticeable problems that keep it from the good range. First, the presentation of the tables is messy and repetitive, which makes the section harder to read than the sample format. Second, the text refers to tables in a somewhat confusing way and skips a clearly presented demographics table in clean form. Third, there is a mismatch in the normality reporting: the narrative says normality was not violated, but the included table shows one Shapiro-Wilk p-value of .024, which would indicate a violation for one cell. In addition, Table 4 includes age effects that were never introduced in the Methods or Results narrative as part of the planned analysis, which weakens coherence. The reporting is therefore mostly correct and complete, but with some inconsistencies and formatting issues. That fits an adequate score rather than a good one.
results_rubric_feedback: The Results rubric appropriately uses the sample results as an anchor and rightly emphasizes completeness and relevance to the stated design. It would be even stronger if it more explicitly separated statistical correctness from presentation quality, because a section can be analytically adequate but poorly formatted. The rubric could also clarify how to handle internal inconsistencies between narrative text and tables, which are common in student work and important for grading. Finally, the expectation of 'roughly three tables' is useful, but it may help to specify the essential content rather than approximate quantity, so assessors focus on function over format.
discussion_feedback: The Discussion is one of the stronger sections. It begins with a clear restatement of the aim and hypotheses, directly answers the research question, and distinguishes between supported and unsupported expectations. The student meaningfully interprets the main pattern of findings rather than merely repeating the results. There is also a real effort to link the findings back to inhibitory learning theory and to prior work, especially Kampmann et al. and Anderson et al. The unexpected absence of a difference between group and individual VR is addressed explicitly, which is important and well done. The section also includes study-specific limitations rather than only generic ones, particularly the concern that the group manipulation may not actually have activated the intended interpersonal mechanisms. Future research suggestions largely follow from these limitations, and the paper ends by reconnecting to broader practical relevance. These features fit the good band. The main reason this section does not score higher is that some interpretations are still somewhat speculative and not always tightly grounded in what was actually manipulated or measured. The theoretical implications are discussed, but not at a very deep level, and the paper sometimes defends the study's conclusions a bit too confidently given the methodological limitations. The second limitation about age is plausible, but more inferential than directly supported by the study. Overall, though, the Discussion is coherent, study-specific, linked to the introduction, and meaningfully interpretive.
discussion_rubric_feedback: The Discussion rubric is strong because it prioritizes interpretation, linkage to theory, comparison with prior research, and study-specific critical reflection. A useful refinement would be to distinguish more clearly between superficial theory linkage and genuinely using theory to explain unexpected findings, since that is often the key marker between adequate and good work. It may also help to specify how much speculative interpretation is acceptable at this level, as student discussions often contain plausible but weakly evidenced explanations. The current wording broadly supports fair assessment, but a few concrete examples of study-specific versus generic limitations would further improve calibration.
lang_style_feedback: The paper is generally understandable and organized into the expected sections, with mostly clear paragraph-level structure and readable scientific prose. Terminology is usually consistent enough to follow the argument. However, there are enough language, style, and APA issues to place this below the satisfactory range. There are recurring grammar and phrasing problems, including awkward sentence construction, punctuation issues, agreement errors, and unclear wording in several places. Some sentences are overly long or imprecise, and a few formulations obscure meaning temporarily. APA style is inconsistent in multiple references and in-text citations, with several formatting errors, capitalization issues, spacing/punctuation inconsistencies, and questionable source formatting. The Results tables are also presented in a very untidy layout that affects readability. There is some redundancy, especially in the Introduction and in the repeated table text. These issues do not make the paper incomprehensible, but they occur often enough that the overall language and style are only developing rather than clearly satisfactory.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: The Language & Style rubric is detailed and practical, especially in warning assessors not to let language errors lower content grades. One improvement would be to reduce reliance on counting errors alone, because not all grammar or APA errors equally affect readability. A stronger distinction between 'readability/clarity' and 'formal APA correctness' could make grading more precise. In addition, the rubric could mention table/figure formatting and integration more explicitly, since presentation quality in these elements can substantially affect comprehensibility even when prose is acceptable.

intro_feedback: De introductie bevat een duidelijke maatschappelijke relevantie, benoemt kernbegrippen, bespreekt passende theorieën en bouwt redelijk logisch toe naar een concrete onderzoeksvraag en hypothese. Positief is dat de verplichte studies van Anderson, Kampmann en Bouchard zijn opgenomen en dat de adolescentendoelgroep expliciet als kennislacune wordt gepositioneerd. Ook is er zichtbaar geprobeerd om theorie, eerdere literatuur en designkeuzes met elkaar te verbinden. Tegelijk blijft de argumentatielijn niet overal even strak. Sommige theoretische claims zijn te stellig of simplistisch geformuleerd, bijvoorbeeld over VRET als vooral gedragsmatig en CGT als vooral cognitief, terwijl de relatie tussen beide behandelingen conceptueel genuanceerder ligt. Daarnaast is de literatuurbespreking soms meer samenvattend dan synthetiserend, en zijn enkele formuleringen inhoudelijk of logisch wat onnauwkeurig. Desondanks is de introductie op dit niveau coherent en relevant, en duidelijk sterker dan slechts adequaat.
intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is sterk doordat zij de kern van wetenschappelijke redenering centraal stelt: lijn naar relevantie, RQ en hypothese. Wel zou de rubric nog bruikbaarder worden als explicieter onderscheid wordt gemaakt tussen samenvatten van literatuur en synthetiseren van literatuur, omdat dat in dit soort opdrachten een belangrijk kwaliteitsverschil is. Ook zou een expliciete verwijzing naar de aansluiting tussen theorie, doelgroep en design de beoordelingsbetrouwbaarheid kunnen vergroten.
methods_feedback: De methodesectie beschrijft een coherent gerandomiseerd design dat aansluit bij de onderzoeksvraag. De deelnemers, globale inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, randomisatie en de twee behandelcondities worden genoemd. Ook zijn kerninstrumenten opgenomen. Daarmee is de sectie in de basis voldoende bruikbaar. Wel ontbreken meerdere details die volgens de schrijfwijzer belangrijk zijn voor volledigheid en reproduceerbaarheid. Zo is de randomisatieprocedure te globaal, blijft onduidelijk hoe de sessies precies verliepen, hoe follow-up-afname werd georganiseerd, wie welke metingen uitvoerde, en hoe therapeuten over condities verdeeld waren. Bij de materialen staan procedurele elementen door elkaar heen met beschrijvingen van interventies. De beschrijving van de LSAS-CA is deels bruikbaar, maar niet volledig consistent uitgewerkt volgens de vereiste vaste onderdelen. Ook ontbreekt een aparte analysesubsectie, terwijl de gekozen analyse pas in Results expliciet wordt genoemd. De methode is dus coherent, maar inhoudelijk nog net niet volledig genoeg voor een hogere beoordeling.
methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek is functioneel, maar relatief globaal. Begrippen als 'compleet' en 'correct' laten veel interpretatieruimte. Voor studentpapers op dit niveau zou het helpen als de rubric explicieter benoemt welke minimale elementen per subkop verplicht zijn, zoals allocatie, inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, demografie, interventiebeschrijving, meetinstrumentdetails en analysegedeelte. Dat maakt het makkelijker om consistent onderscheid te maken tussen ontwikkelend, adequaat en goed.
results_feedback: De resultaten volgen gedeeltelijk de verwachte structuur met een korte opening, descriptieve tabellen, een mixed ANOVA en post-hocvergelijkingen. Dat is positief. Toch zijn er belangrijke tekortkomingen die deze sectie sterk beperken. De rapportage is incompleet: cruciale vrijheidsgraden ontbreken bij alle F-tests, tabellen zijn niet correct uitgewerkt in lopende vorm, en de resultatenverwijzing naar tabellen en figuur wordt niet goed ondersteund door een nette presentatie. Er is bovendien een duidelijke inconsistentie tussen de beschreven follow-up in de methode (12 maanden) en de tekst in de resultaten, waar ook over drie maanden follow-up wordt gesproken. Verder is de interpretatie van het interactiepatroon niet volledig helder en wordt het verschil tussen condities op follow-up niet rechtstreeks gerapporteerd, terwijl dat juist belangrijk is voor de hypothese. De analyse lijkt in grote lijnen passend bij het design, maar de verslaglegging is te onvolledig en te inconsistent om hoger dan minimaal voldoende te scoren.
results_rubric_feedback: De resultatenrubriek benoemt relevantie en correctheid, maar kan scherper operationaliseren wat 'compleet' inhoudt bij deze opdracht. Gezien de voorbeeldsectie lijkt er een impliciete verwachting te zijn van descriptieve tabellen, assumptiechecks, volledige teststatistieken en post-hocrapportage. Als die verwachtingen expliciet in de rubric staan, wordt de beoordeling transparanter en consistenter. Ook zou het nuttig zijn om onderscheid te maken tussen passende analysekeuze en kwaliteit van statistische verslaglegging.
discussion_feedback: De discussie begint sterk met een duidelijke terugkoppeling naar doel, onderzoeksvraag en hypothese. De student interpreteert de korte- en langetermijnbevindingen expliciet en probeert deze systematisch te relateren aan eerdere literatuur en aan de twee theoretische perspectieven. Ook bevat de sectie relevante beperkingen, concrete voorstellen voor vervolgonderzoek en een terugkeer naar maatschappelijke implicaties. Dat past goed bij de opdracht. Tegelijk is de discussie niet overal even zorgvuldig. Er zitten enkele inhoudelijke inconsistenties in de interpretatie van de resultaten, vooral rond de lange termijn: enerzijds wordt gesteld dat het VRET-effect niet blijvend is, anderzijds wordt ook gezegd dat de afname van pre tot follow-up juist groter was in die conditie. Deze spanning wordt niet volledig uitgewerkt. Daarnaast zijn sommige verklaringen speculatief of te sterk geformuleerd gegeven de data. De discussie is dus inhoudelijk behoorlijk en duidelijk boven ontwikkelingsniveau, maar mist de consistentie en precisie voor een hogere score.
discussion_rubric_feedback: De discussierubriek legt terecht nadruk op hoofdconclusie en kritische reflectie. Een mogelijke verbetering is om explicieter te vermelden dat interne consistentie binnen de interpretatie van resultaten meeweegt: studenten kunnen immers wel veel onderdelen noemen, maar toch tegenstrijdige conclusies trekken. Ook zou een apart criterium voor de kwaliteit van de koppeling tussen resultaten, theorie en eerdere literatuur de rubric verder versterken.
lang_style_feedback: De tekst is over het algemeen goed leesbaar en de wetenschappelijke schrijfstijl is meestal passend voor dit niveau. De opbouw per sectie is herkenbaar en de lezer kan de grote lijn meestal volgen. Wel zijn er geregeld grammaticale fouten, formuleringen die stroef of onnatuurlijk zijn, inconsistent gebruik van termen, en APA-onzuiverheden in zowel tekst als referentielijst. Ook zijn er meerdere slordigheden zoals wisselend gebruik van afkortingen, interpunctieproblemen, kleine stijlbreuken tussen Nederlands en Engels, en zinnen die inhoudelijk net niet precies zijn. De structuur is dus meestal duidelijk, maar de afwerking is niet sterk genoeg voor een hogere beoordeling.
lang_style_rubric_feedback: De rubric voor taal en stijl is bruikbaar, maar combineert veel verschillende dimensies in één criterium: taalbeheersing, structuur, APA, vaagheid en redundantie. Daardoor kan het lastig zijn om precies te wegen waar een score op gebaseerd is. Voor meer beoordelingsconsistentie zou het helpen om minstens een onderscheid te maken tussen helderheid/structuur enerzijds en formele afwerking/APA anderzijds.

intro_feedback: De inleiding heeft een duidelijke maatschappelijke relevantie, benoemt een concrete kennislacune en werkt toe naar een heldere onderzoeksvraag en hypothese. Positief is dat meerdere studies als bouwstenen worden gebruikt en dat theorie expliciet wordt gekoppeld aan het verwachte effect van exposure en de combinatie van VRET met CGT. Ook wordt de keuze voor adolescenten en een follow-upmeting goed gemotiveerd. De lijn van redeneren is daardoor overwegend coherent en relevant. Wel zijn er enkele zwakkere punten die verhinderen dat dit hoger uitkomt. De theoretische uitwerking is soms wat stellig of simplificerend, bijvoorbeeld in de tegenstelling tussen VRET als vooral gedragsmatig en CGT als vooral cognitief, terwijl beide behandelingen in de praktijk minder scherp gescheiden zijn. Daarnaast is de synthese van de literatuur niet altijd helemaal nauwkeurig en soms meer beschrijvend dan analytisch. Er zitten ook enkele onzorgvuldigheden in formulering en brongebruik, zoals inconsistenties in namen, jaartallen en claims over specifieke bevindingen. Maar binnen het niveau van tweedejaarsstudenten is dit een bovengemiddelde introductie met een herkenbare argumentatieve opbouw.
intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is inhoudelijk sterk omdat zij de kern van wetenschappelijke redenering centraal stelt: lijn van argumentatie, relevantie, RQ en verantwoord brongebruik. Een mogelijk verbeterpunt is dat het onderscheid tussen ‘adequate’, ‘good’ en ‘excellent’ nu vooral in termen van coherentie en overtuigingskracht is geformuleerd, waardoor beoordelaars relatief veel interpretatieruimte hebben. Het zou helpen om explicieter te maken hoe literatuursynthese, theoretische inbedding en de zichtbaarheid van de kennislacune meewegen binnen deze niveaus.
methods_feedback: De methode beschrijft een coherent gerandomiseerd ontwerp dat goed aansluit op de onderzoeksvraag. De deelnemers, inclusie- en exclusiecriteria, globale werving en randomisatie worden genoemd, en de twee condities zijn op hoofdlijnen voldoende onderscheidbaar. Ook is het positief dat de student een concreet meetinstrument kiest en de interventies probeert te standaardiseren qua sessieduur en protocol. Toch zijn er meerdere onvolledigheden die de repliceerbaarheid beperken. De procedure is erg kort en bevat weinig chronologische detail over wat deelnemers precies doen, wanneer de sessies plaatsvinden, hoe lang de follow-upinterval precies is ingebed, wie welke metingen afneemt, en hoe de randomisatie praktisch is uitgevoerd. In de materialen staan relevante onderdelen deels vermengd, en de beschrijving van de LSAS-CA is niet volledig consistent met de operationalisatie. Ook ontbreekt informatie over beloning en toewijzing op een meer precieze manier, en er is geen aparte analysemethode beschreven in de methode zelf. Daarmee is de methode wel adequaat en begrijpelijk, maar nog niet volledig genoeg voor een sterkere beoordeling.
methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek benoemt terecht coherentie tussen design, RQ en hypothesen, plus volledigheid en begrijpelijkheid van deelnemers, materialen en procedure. Een verbetering zou zijn om nog explicieter te operationaliseren wat ‘compleet’ betekent op cursusniveau, bijvoorbeeld door kernonderdelen zoals inclusie/exclusie, randomisatie, meetmomenten en voldoende detail voor repliceerbaarheid te noemen. Dat zou de aansluiting op de writing guide nog directer maken en de interbeoordelaarsbetrouwbaarheid vergroten.
results_feedback: De resultatensectie volgt globaal de verwachte structuur met een korte openingszin, assumpties, ANOVA, post-hoc-vergelijkingen en verwijzingen naar tabellen en een figuur. Dat sluit aan bij het voorbeeld uit de cursus. Het grootste probleem is echter de onvolledigheid en inconsistentie van de rapportage. Cruciale statistische informatie ontbreekt, zoals vrijheidsgraden in de F-tests, en de tabellen zijn in de lopende tekst niet goed uitgewerkt of volledig gepresenteerd. Er is bovendien een belangrijke inconsistentie tussen de beschreven meetmomenten: in de methode is sprake van een 12-maanden follow-up, terwijl in de resultaten ook “drie maanden follow-up” staat. De descriptieve data onderaan zijn slordig weergegeven en niet in een duidelijk tabelformat geïntegreerd. Verder is de rapportage van p-waarden soms onjuist geformuleerd (bijvoorbeeld p = < .001). Hoewel de gekozen analyse passend lijkt bij het design en de interpretatie van het interactie-effect in grote lijnen begrijpelijk is, is de sectie als geheel te incompleet en te inconsistent om ruim boven de ondergrens uit te komen. Daarom is dit net voldoende.
results_rubric_feedback: De resultatenrubriek is functioneel, maar blijft vrij globaal. Zeker voor beginnende studenten is het nuttig dat er aanvullend een sample results section is, omdat de rubric zelf weinig concreet maakt wat ‘compleet’ of ‘coherent’ precies inhoudt. Het zou helpen als de rubric expliciet zou verwijzen naar minimale elementen zoals descriptieve tabellen, rapportage van de hoofdanalyse, assumptiechecks en post-hocvergelijkingen. Daarmee wordt de verwachting transparanter en wordt onderscheid tussen een net-voldoende en goede resultssectie makkelijker.
discussion_feedback: De discussie heeft een duidelijke openingsparagraaf waarin de onderzoeksvraag, hypothese en hoofdbevindingen worden samengevat. Dat maakt de redenering deels intern inconsistent. Ook zijn sommige verklaringen speculatief of te stellig, en de koppeling aan theorie is aanwezig maar niet altijd scherp uitgewerkt in termen van wat precies wel of niet is getoetst. Desondanks laat deze discussie op studentniveau duidelijk wetenschappelijk redeneren zien en is zij gemiddeld tot licht bovengemiddeld.

intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is sterk doordat zij de kern van deze cursus goed centraal zet: de lijn van redenering naar relevantie, RQ en hypothese. methods_feedback: De methode is in de basis coherent en passend bij de onderzoeksvraag: er is een gerandomiseerd design met twee behandelcondities en drie meetmomenten, wat goed aansluit op de hypothese over langetermijneffecten. methods_rubric_feedback: De methoderubriek benadrukt terecht coherentie tussen design en onderzoeksvraag. results_feedback: De resultaten volgen globaal de gewenste structuur met een openingszin, verwijzing naar tabellen, een mixed ANOVA en post-hocvergelijkingen. Voor dit niveau hoeft statistiek niet perfect te zijn, maar de onvolledigheid en inconsistenties maken deze sectie slechts net voldoende.

discussion_rubric_feedback: De discussierubriek sluit goed aan bij het leerdoel van wetenschappelijke argumentatie en kritische reflectie. intro_rubric_feedback: De introductierubriek is inhoudelijk sterk omdat zij de nadruk legt op argumentatieve lijn, synthese en aansluiting op de onderzoeksvraag in plaats van alleen op aanwezigheid van literatuur.
